findings.citation: E. Guendelman, D. Singleton, 'Momentum Gauge Fields and Non-Commutative Space-Time', Symmetry 15 (2023) 126, arXiv:2206.02638.
findings.summary: The paper applies the gauge principle to x = i hbar d/dp, which introduces a momentum-space gauge field C(p) with its own coupling g. The authors call this 'a dynamical version of Born's reciprocity theory' and say Born reciprocity 'would imply that for every ordinary gauge field there should be a corresponding momentum gauge field'. They ask whether g and e satisfy 'something like the Dirac quantization condition' between electric and magnetic charge, or are exchanged by Born reciprocity (e <-> g), and leave the question open. In the program's terms a gauge field local in momentum is the natural gauge field of a p-polarized sector. There is no separate p-polarized matter sector and no magnetically charged particle, and the Dirac-type relation is a question, not a claim. There is no dark matter. findings.difference: The momentum-space charges are electric under the momentum gauge field, the opposite of C4's assignment. There is no matter sector and no magnetic analog of our charges.

findings.summary: A Born-reciprocal ('trans-Planckian') model with independent metrics and U(1) gauge fields on the position and momentum manifolds, and a matter field identified with dark matter.
findings.difference: The momentum-manifold gauge field is explicitly not electromagnetism: a universal 'graviphoton'. There is no magnetic charge. Its dark-matter and acceleration claims bear on C1 and C5, not C4.

findings.citation: J. Terning, C. B. Verhaaren, 'Dark Monopoles and SL(2,Z) Duality', JHEP 12 (2018) 123, arXiv:1808.09459.
findings.summary: Kinetic mixing between two Abelian gauge theories, each with electric and magnetic charges. When one photon is massive, particles of one sector get parametrically small couplings to the other's photon, and the surviving duality is the diagonal SL(2,Z). This bears on how C4's separate-photon form would relate to its shared-photon form: the electric/magnetic assignment of a hidden sector becomes physical relative to ours only through mixing.
findings.difference: There is no position-momentum structure and no full mirror family; strict P4 forbids the mixing.

quotes.text: including the failure of Dirac charge quantization as particles from one sector obtain parametrically small couplings to the photon of the other
which is the diagonal subgroup of the dualities of the two un-mixed gauge theories

findings.citation: J. Terning, C. B. Verhaaren, 'Detecting Dark Matter with Aharonov-Bohm', JHEP 12 (2019) 152, arXiv:1906.00014.
findings.summary: Dark-U(1) monopoles acquire small magnetic couplings to our photon through kinetic mixing (below the dark photon mass), are bound by dark flux tubes, and could be seen by Aharonov-Bohm phases. This is dark matter carrying a small magnetic charge of our photon.
findings.difference: The charges are small, confined and in position space. There is no mirror family and no momentum polarization.

quotes.text: Magnetic monopoles of the dark $U(1)_D$ can obtain small magnetic couplings to our photon through this kinetic mixing.

findings.citation: F. Brümmer, J. Jaeckel, 'Minicharges and Magnetic Monopoles', Phys. Lett. B 675 (2009) 360, arXiv:0902.3615.
findings.summary: With kinetic mixing between our U(1) and a hidden U(1), angular-momentum quantization allows only certain combinations of ordinary and hidden monopole charge. This constrains any scheme in which a hidden sector's magnetic charges are related to ours.
findings.difference: Constrains charge assignments; it does not propose a magnetic mirror.

quotes.text: We find that angular momentum quantization allows only certain combinations of ordinary and hidden monopole charge.

findings.citation: T. Hiramatsu, M. Ibe, M. Suzuki, S. Yamaguchi, 'Gauge kinetic mixing and dark topological defects', JHEP 12 (2021) 122, arXiv:2109.12771.
findings.summary: With a massless dark photon kinetically mixed with ours, a dark monopole induces no QED magnetic flux. So a separate-photon sector does not become a shared-photon one through mixing alone; with a massive dark photon ('bead' configurations) a pseudo-monopole flux appears.
findings.difference: A statement about hidden-sector defects; there is no mirror family and no momentum polarization.

quotes.text: The dark monopole, on the other hand, does not induce the QED magnetic flux in the U(1) symmetric phase, even in the presence of the kinetic mixing.

findings.citation: M. L. Graesser, I. M. Shoemaker, N. Tapia Arellano, 'Milli-magnetic monopole dark matter and the survival of galactic magnetic fields', JHEP 03 (2022) 105, arXiv:2105.05769.
findings.summary: Monopoles of a broken dark U(1) appear in our sector as confined milli-magnetically charged objects. As dark matter they are bounded by halo ellipticity and by an extended Parker bound.
findings.difference: The charges are small, not Dirac charges of our photon, and there is no mirror family or momentum polarization. Its Parker-type analysis is the kind the shared-photon form must pass.

quotes.text: will appear in our sector as confined milli-magnetically charged objects under ordinary electromagnetism

findings.citation: A. Hook, J. Huang, 'Bounding millimagnetically charged particles with magnetars', Phys. Rev. D 96 (2017) 055010, arXiv:1705.01107.
findings.summary: Milli-magnetic charges arise generically with kinetic mixing. Schwinger pair production at magnetars bounds them below 10^-18 over a wide mass range.
findings.difference: It bounds small magnetic charges of light particles; it does not test full-strength analogs or a momentum polarization.

quotes.text: Milli-magnetically charged particles generically appear in scenarios with kinetic mixing.

findings.citation: J. Scott, T. J. Evans, D. Singleton, V. Dzhunushaliev, V. Folomeev, 'Dirac and non-Dirac conditions in the two-potential theory of magnetic charge', Eur. Phys. J. C 78 (2018) 382, arXiv:1805.09649.
findings.summary: In the Cabibbo-Ferrari two-potential theory, if only one kind of charged field is present a duality rotation removes either the electric or the magnetic charge. This bears on the separate-photon form: a sector whose particles are only magnetic under its own photon is, by that photon's duality, equivalent to one with electric charges at the dual coupling. 'Magnetic' is physical only relative to another charge of the same photon, or through mixing with ours.
findings.difference: A general point about two-potential theories, not a proposal of a mirror sector.

quotes.text: With only one field one can always use a duality rotation to rotate away either the electric or magnetic charge, and thus decouple either the associated electric or magnetic photon.

findings.citation: D. Singleton, 'Magnetic charge as a "hidden" gauge symmetry', Int. J. Theor. Phys. 34 (1995) 37, arXiv:hep-th/9701044.
findings.summary: A two-potential theory with a second 'magnetic' photon, made massive by a Higgs mechanism so that magnetic charge and its symmetry are hidden at low energy. This is an early way of hiding the magnetic half of electromagnetism.
findings.difference: The magnetic half is hidden by a mass gap, not placed in a conjugate polarization, and nothing is said about dark matter.

quotes.text: This problem is dealt with by using the Higgs mechanism to give a mass to one of the gauge bosons while the other remains massless.

findings.citation: S. Carneiro, 'Dual symmetry breaking and magnetic charge screening', arXiv:2609.25324 (preprint).
findings.summary: In dual electrodynamics with electric and magnetic Higgs fields, a vacuum in which only the magnetic scalar condenses screens magnetic charge but not electric charge. A vacuum thus picks the electric description, and the screened monopole is offered as a dark-sector candidate whose long-range signature, and hence the usual Parker-type bounds, are removed. This bears on the 'one vacuum event selects the electric sublattice' clause and is a third way, besides p-localization and binding, of hiding magnetic charges of our photon.
findings.difference: The vacuum selects the duality frame only, not a phase-space polarization of matter. It has no position-momentum structure and no mirror family. Preprint.

quotes.text: The broken phase contains a natural dark sector candidate: the screened monopole.

findings.citation: J. A. Harvey, S. Jensen, 'Worldsheet instanton corrections to the Kaluza-Klein monopole', JHEP 10 (2005) 028, arXiv:hep-th/0507204; see also S. Jensen, JHEP 07 (2011) 088, arXiv:1106.1174.
findings.summary: The Kaluza-Klein monopole, a magnetic object and the T-dual of the NS5-brane, is localized in winding space, the coordinate dual to position under T-duality, and is probed only by strings with winding charge. This is a published case of a magnetic object hidden from position-space probes by localization in a dual coordinate, the kind of hiding the shared-photon form needs.
findings.difference: T-duality maps a magnetic object (NS5) to a magnetic object (KK monopole), not electric to magnetic. The magnetic charge is under the Kaluza-Klein gauge field, not our photon. It bears more directly on C2-C3.

quotes.text: These corrections can be understood as a localization in winding space which could be probed by strings with winding charge around the circle.

closest.why: Closest to the whole conjecture: the only paper found that uses the reciprocity structure of Born geometry (the metastring's eta pairing) to make the gauge group of the dual-coordinate, 'dark' sector the electric-magnetic (Langlands) dual of the visible one. It differs as follows. It concerns gauge groups, not magnetically charged matter. For E8 the authors call the two 'physically indistinguishable'. The dual sector is the T-dual coordinate space x~, not a spontaneously selected momentum polarization. There is no photon, no coupling relation, no shared-photon form and no monopole.

Closest to the separate-photon form. The dark matter is monopoles magnetic under their own 'extraordinary' photon, ordinary matter is electrons under ours, and a Schwinger condition ties the couplings. It differs in having no position-momentum or reciprocity structure, a single electron-monopole pair instead of a mirror family, and kinetic mixing, which strict P4 forbids. Preprint.

Closest to the shared-photon form. It asks whether 'a dark parallel world of purely magnetically charged matter', magnetic under (dual) electromagnetism and gravitating, could be the dark matter. It differs in that its darkness comes from the action-derived Lorentz force, not from localization in momentum; it has no Born reciprocity and no per-particle mirror, and is posed as a question.

Closest to the bridge behind C4 (#11 §11.3): 'electric-magnetic duality is a special case of Born-Reciprocity', Born reciprocity in strings gives T-duality, and T and S sit inside U-duality. It differs in being a remark about the field phase space (B, D) that makes no claim about charges, couplings or a matter sector.

search.notes:
No paper found anticipates C4. Its two halves have separate prior art, and the combination (the magnetic counterparts of our electric particles placed in the momentum polarization) was not found.
(1) The bridge behind C4, #11 §11.3, is published as a remark. Gibbons and Herdeiro (PRD 2001) wrote that 'electric-magnetic duality is a special case of Born-Reciprocity', that Born reciprocity in strings gives T-duality, and that T and S sit inside U-duality. Russo and Townsend (JHEP 2025) repeat it. Technically, S-duality reduces to T-duality (Harvey-Moore-Strominger 1995; Kapustin-Witten 2006), is a canonical transformation (Lozano 1995), or is perturbatively a Fourier transform (Galakhov-Mironov-Morozov). The record tags the identification [D - structural; math T] and cites none of these, so §11.3 should credit them.
(2) The magnetic half of electromagnetism as a dark sector is published without any momentum structure. Vento 2025 is the separate-photon form (dark-matter monopoles under their own photon, preprint), and Govaerts (EPJC 2023) asks the shared-photon-like question (a dark parallel world of magnetically charged matter).
(3) Berglund, Hübsch and Minic (2021; IJMPD 2023) are the only ones found to join Born geometry, a dual/'dark' sector and electric-magnetic (Langlands) duality, at the level of gauge groups and with no physical consequence for E8.
(4) A finding against the conjecture's intuition. Wherever Born's rho is applied to electromagnetism in the literature (Szabo 2019; Lüst-Malek-Szabo 2017; Bakas-Lüst 2013; Bérard-Mohrbach 2004; Pan-Yin 2024; Copinger-Morales 2023), it keeps electric with electric(-like) and magnetic with magnetic(-like): a magnetic charge in position space maps to a magnetic-type object over momentum space (R-flux, a dual monopole, a Berry monopole). It does not map electric charge to magnetic charge. Only the T-duality / worldsheet reading puts the dual momentum with the magnetic charge (Harvey-Moore-Strominger; FLM 2013's 2d dyon picture, which is in the record's own reference [3]). Riello 2017 has the opposite assignment in field phase space.
(5) Scott et al. 2018 and Terning-Verhaaren 2018 show that a separate sector whose particles are only magnetic under its own photon is, by that photon's duality, an electric sector at the dual coupling. 'Magnetic' becomes physical only relative to ours, through mixing or shared charges, which strict P4 excludes. This sharpens what the separate-photon form can claim.
Cross-group notes. Vento 2025 and Govaerts 2023 also bear on C1 (dark matter as a mirror sector) and C3 (the null result). Harvey-Jensen 2005 (KK monopole localized in winding space), Szabo 2019 and Lüst-Malek-Szabo 2017 (R-flux as momentum-space magnetic charge) bear on C2-C3. Brümmer, Ferrante, Fischer, Frigerio 2025 (PRD 113 (2026) L091701, arXiv:2509.21924: the stable W' of a minimal dark 't Hooft-Polyakov sector always outweighs the monopoles) is published support for #11 §12's W'-overclosure finding and bears on C2. Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2020 (LHEP 2021 186: dark matter from the degrees of freedom dual to visible matter) and Bolognesi 2009/2015 bear on C1, C5 and the program's core. 'Magnetic dark matter' in HEP usually means dark matter with a magnetic dipole moment (Del Nobile et al., JCAP 08 (2012) 010, arXiv:1203.6652), another collision.
Method: 98 logged lit.py queries (INSPIRE title/abstract and full text, citation graph forward and backward, arXiv API, Crossref), 3 WebSearch queries, WebFetch for PDFs that lit.py cannot reach (Pan-Yin, Harvey-Moore-Strominger, Kapustin-Witten, Ginsparg, Born 1949), with text extracted locally (work/literature-check/g3-magnetic-mirror/pdf/). Every quote was re-checked by lit.py quote when the output file was built: 65 FOUND, 4 checked against PDF text. verdicts.reason: Metadata match (conference paper; INSPIRE conference record 1886350: Nankai Symposium on Mathematical Dialogues, online, opened 2021-08-02; IJMPD 32 (2023) 2330002 for 2212.06086). The search summary misreads the construction. The Langlands ('electro-magnetic') duality relates the heterotic string's two E8 factors, which BHM generate from the internal coordinates x^18..25 and their duals x~^18..25. Both factors are standard, x-dependent fields: 'we have both the standard A_mu^alpha(x), A_mu^alpha~(x), as well as their ("dark") duals' (2212.06086 §6, FOUND), and each dark x~-dependent dual is 'valued in the same E8 algebra' (FOUND). The dark sector therefore carries both groups, as the visible one does; it is not the electromagnetic dual of ours. The nearest point to C4 is item 4, a correlation term pairing visible E8 fields with dark E8~ fields through eta, and the same term with the groups swapped. The authors call the two E8s 'physically indistinguishable'. What the paper states is the mechanism behind C4, in the program's own Born-geometry lineage: the eta pairing of x with x~ makes the gauge groups they generate each other's Langlands (e-m) duals. That is prior art for #11 §11.3's identification, not for §11.4's mirror. It has no matter, charges, photon, coupling relation or monopoles.

Confirmed in the Conclusions. With the Lorentz force derived from his action, electric and magnetic matter form 'mutually electromagnetically "dark" sectors', and Govaerts asks whether this gives a dark-matter candidate: 'a dark parallel world of purely magnetically charged matter' that contributes to the energy-momentum tensor. This is a close variant of the shared-photon form: the magnetic half of (dual) electrodynamics as a dark, gravitating parallel world of matter. It is posed as a question. Differences, as the searcher states: no position-momentum structure (the darkness comes from the force law, not from localization in momentum), no per-particle mirror, no model of spectrum, abundance or Parker-bound status.

Confirmed (abstract, §2). The ordinary photon couples only to electric charge and the 'extraordinary' photon only to magnetic charge; monopoles plus the extraordinary photon are the dark sector, electrons plus the ordinary photon the visible one; the Schwinger condition eg/sqrt(1-eps^2) = n ties the dark magnetic coupling to e. A variant of the separate-photon form (dark analogs magnetic under their own photon, coupling Dirac-tied to ours). Vento frames it as a generalization of QED, so it also reads as the magnetic half of QED made dark. Differences: one electron-monopole pair, not a mirror family; a kinetic-mixing portal, which strict P4 excludes; position space; no reciprocity. Preprint, v3 of 2026-01-07 (arXiv API); García-Moreno and Vento 2610.02083 confirmed.

Downgraded. §1 makes a remark: 'electric-magnetic duality is a special case of Born-Reciprocity', a rotation (p,q) -> (p cos t + q sin t, q cos t - p sin t) of the phase space of nonlinear electrodynamics with B and D as the conjugate pair; then 'Born reciprocity applied to string theory gives rise to T-duality' and T and S inside U-duality. This is the mechanism behind C4, #11 §11.3's identification and its T/S/U analogy, and §11.3 should cite it: the record tags the identification [D — structural; math T] and the U-duality analogy [T] without a citation. It is not the conjecture: the rotation acts on the field phase space (B, D), not on spacetime position and momentum, and nothing is said about matter, magnetic analogs or a momentum polarization. Under the brief's labels a paper that states the mechanism but not the conjecture is 'related'.

Downgraded. One sentence in the Conclusions: the Z2 duality group left in the quantum theory of self-dual NLED 'is an example of Born-reciprocity' (citing Born 1938 and FLM 2014). The same mechanism-level identification as Gibbons-Herdeiro, about the duality of the Maxwell field; nothing on charges, matter or polarization.

Downgraded. The momentum gauge field C(p) couples to ordinary particles through x -> x - gC(p), an electric-type minimal coupling in momentum space, not a magnetic charge. Born reciprocity is invoked to pair every gauge field with a momentum gauge field, and a Dirac-like relation between e and g is raised as a question and left ('We leave this question for future work'). No second matter sector, no magnetic analogs, no dark matter. It shares the mechanism (reciprocity applied to the gauge principle; a coupling relation), so 'related'.

Confirmed: the abstract gives F <= 1e-16 (m/1e17 GeV) cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1 and excludes monopoles much lighter than 1e17 GeV as the closure density. It weighs against the shared-photon form only where the analogs act as position-localized monopoles of our photon at dark-matter density, the case #11 §11.4 already flags. It is silent on the separate-photon form and on objects whose field profile is spread in position.

Confirmed in context: the worldsheet Coulomb-gas picture of vertex correlators 'generalizes to 2d electromagnetism with electric and magnetic charges (dyons)' when vertices carry both p and p-bar, and DSZ quantization equals the diffeomorphism constraint. Dual momentum plays the magnetic charge, but on the worldsheet, not in spacetime matter. Relevant because it is the record's own reference [3].

new_findings.summary: An electric charge near the surface of a topological insulator induces an image magnetic monopole through the topological magnetoelectric effect. A 2019 experiment calls it 'an induced mirror magnetic monopole'. In words: every electric charge has a magnetic mirror image.
new_findings.difference: An image field of a material's electromagnetic response (axion electrodynamics), not a magnetically charged particle and not a second matter sector. A reader searching 'electric charge', 'mirror' and 'magnetic monopole' meets it first.

new_findings.citation: J. Polchinski, 'Monopoles, duality, and string theory', Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 19S1 (2004) 145, arXiv:hep-th/0304042 (conference proceedings, Dirac Centennial Symposium, 2002).
new_findings.summary: Two 'principles of completeness': where charge is quantized, magnetic monopoles exist; and in a fully unified theory every gauge field has both electric and magnetic sources with the minimal Dirac quantum. This is the premise of the shared-photon form and of C3: magnetic charges of our own photon should exist somewhere.
new_findings.difference: Says nothing about where the magnetic sources are: no second sector, no momentum polarization, no dark matter. Polchinski calls both principles aesthetic, not theorems. The record states only Dirac's direction (magnetic charge implies quantization, #11 §11.4), not this converse.

not_found_assessment.reason: Statement 1 (a matter sector related to ours by a position-momentum exchange whose particles are the magnetic counterparts of our electric ones). Holds. None of my 31 lit.py queries, 3 WebSearch queries or citation sweeps found it, and on reading, the searcher's closest paper does not state it either: in Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021 the dark x~-dependent fields carry the same algebras as the visible ones, and the Langlands (e-m) duality relates the two heterotic E8 factors. The closest papers are now Govaerts 2023 (a question; shared-photon-like) and Vento 2025 (a model; separate-photon-like), neither with position-momentum structure, and at the level of mechanism Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021 and Gibbons-Herdeiro 2000.

Statement 2 (shared-photon form with the magnetic charges of our photon hidden by localization in momentum). Holds. INSPIRE full text for monopoles plus momentum space plus dark matter plus position space (16 hits), Born reciprocity plus dark matter plus magnetic charge (1), T-dual plus winding plus dark matter plus magnetic charge (4 theses), and two extended WebSearch queries returned nothing on it. The published hiding mechanisms remain screening (Carneiro 2026), the force law of a doubled-potential theory (Govaerts 2023), confinement under mixing (Terning-Verhaaren; Graesser et al.) and winding-space localization of a KK monopole (Harvey-Jensen 2005, not our photon).

Statement 3 (one vacuum event selecting both the position polarization and the electric sublattice). Holds. INSPIRE abstracts joining spontaneous breaking of e-m duality to position, phase space, momentum space or reciprocity: 0 hits; without that restriction, 17 hits, none of which ties a duality-frame choice to a phase-space polarization (by title: Chan and Tsou on Yang-Mills duality as the origin of fermion generations, supersymmetric gauge dynamics, lattice and condensed-matter symmetry breaking). Carneiro 2026 remains nearest: a vacuum selects the electric frame only.

Statement 4 (a conjugate or dark sector whose coupling is fixed at the S-dual of ours by a reciprocity map). Holds. Full-text searches for a dark fine-structure constant with S-duality or Dirac quantization returned 0, 0 and 1 hit (Graesser et al., already listed). The only precedent found for reciprocity fixing a coupling is Born 1940 on Landé's argument that reciprocity gives 137, which concerns our own alpha (new finding, abstract only).

Statement 5 (Born's own reciprocity papers relating reciprocity to magnetic charge). Holds on the evidence available, with a caveat. INSPIRE lists 11 of Born's reciprocity papers (1938-1950); no title mentions magnetic poles. The searcher read Born 1949 (Rev. Mod. Phys.). The abstracts of Born, Cheng and Green 1949, 'Reciprocity Theory of Electrodynamics' (Nature 164, 281), and of Born 1940 on the number 137 contain nothing magnetic. The full texts of Born 1938 (Royal Society: HTTP 403 again; no free copy found by WebSearch), Born 1940 (Cambridge Core, no access) and Born-Cheng-Green 1949 (Nature login) were not read, so for those three the statement rests on abstracts.

verify.notes:
Verification of the searcher's 43 C4 findings. Metadata: every identifier resolves and matches title, authors, year and venue (lit.py show for all 47 identifiers; Crossref for Optica 1 250 and Post 1987; the INSPIRE conference record and arXiv comment for Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021). Quotes: 65/69 FOUND by lit.py; the other 4 (Harvey-Moore-Strominger §1, Kapustin-Witten x2, Pan-Yin) are in arXiv PDFs without HTML, and I confirmed them in my own downloads (pypdf, loose matches from ligatures and line breaks).
Relation changes: four 'partial' become 'related'. (1) Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021: the search summary misreads the paper. The Langlands (e-m) duality relates the heterotic string's two E8 factors, both present as standard fields, and each dark x~-dependent dual is 'valued in the same E8 algebra'; the dark sector is not the electromagnetic dual of ours. (2) Gibbons-Herdeiro 2000 and (3) Russo-Townsend 2025: remarks that e-m duality is a case of Born reciprocity, a rotation of the field phase space (B, D). They state the mechanism behind C4, not the conjecture. (4) Guendelman-Singleton 2022: the momentum gauge field couples by x -> x - gC(p), an electric-type coupling in momentum space, and the Dirac-like relation is a question. Kept: Govaerts 2023 and Vento 2025 as 'partial' (a magnetic dark sector mirroring our electric matter, without position-momentum structure), and Adams et al. 1993 as 'evidence-against' (shared-photon form with position-localized analogs). The other 36 labels are confirmed.
Result for C4: no anticipation. The two partials lack the momentum polarization, which is C4's distinctive content. For the record: #11 §11.3's identification (S-duality and Born's rho as one rotation) and its T/S/U analogy were stated as a remark by Gibbons and Herdeiro (PRD 63 (2001) 064006) and again by Russo and Townsend (2025), and in Born geometry by Berglund, Hübsch and Minic (the eta pairing of x with x~ makes the gauge groups Langlands duals). The record tags the identification [D — structural; math T] and cites none of them.
The searcher's observation (4) holds and gains a case: where rho is applied to electromagnetism, magnetic maps to magnetic-type (Szabo; Lüst-Malek-Szabo; Bakas-Lüst; Bérard-Mohrbach; Pan-Yin; and Martina 2011, arXiv:1110.6906, 'a charged particle simultaneously interacting with a magnetic monopole and a dual monopole in momenta space', FOUND). Gauging under reciprocity gives electric-type couplings in momentum space (Guendelman-Singleton; Copinger-Morales). Only worldsheet and T-duality readings put the dual momentum with the magnetic charge (FLM 2013; Harvey-Moore-Strominger 1995). Scott et al. 2018: with only one kind of charged field a duality rotation removes either the electric or the magnetic charge, so analogs that are magnetic only under their own photon can equally be described as electric under it; the separate-photon form's content then lies in its coupling relation unless the p-sector also has electric charges.
New findings (5): one collision, Qi et al. 2009 (an electric charge induces an image, or 'mirror', magnetic monopole); Polchinski's completeness principles, the premise of the shared-photon form and of C3; Vasconcellos and Hadjimichef 2014, 'dual dark matter' from the photon's dual partner; and two of Born's own reciprocity papers on electromagnetism (Born 1940 on 137; Born, Cheng, Green 1949), abstracts only, with nothing magnetic. All new quotes FOUND by lit.py.
Cross-group leads: Delbourgo and Lashmar, Found. Phys. 38 (2008) 995, arXiv:0709.0776: Born reciprocity with a scale b = m Omega 'might possibly offer an explanation for galactic rotation, without invoking dark matter' (FOUND; C1/C6). Martina 2011 (above) bears on C2.

findings.citation: F. Henry-Couannier, "The dark side of gravity and the acceleration of the universe", 2nd World Summit: Exploring the Dark Side of the Universe (EDSU2018), PoS(EDSU2018)047 (2018); conference proceedings
findings.summary: Dark Gravity treats the metric g and its 'inverse' g̃ = η g⁻¹ η as two faces of one field (a 'Janus field'), each with its own matter. In the cosmological sector the two scale factors are inverses, ã(t) = 1/a(t), and the paper states that our side's expansion means the dark side is contracting. After a postulated discontinuous permutation of the two scale factors at the transition redshift, the dark side's source term dominates and drives our evolution, giving a constantly accelerated expansion a(t′) ~ t′² with no cosmological constant (the paper's single parameter replacing Λ is the transition redshift, predicted 0.78 against a measured 0.67 ± 0.1). Dark-side mass acts on our side as negative mass.
findings.difference: Closest configuration found, but not the same claim. The conjugate world is the inverse metric of a flat-background theory, related to ours by a global time-reversal/permutation symmetry, not the momentum-space (Born-reciprocal) description of our universe. The acceleration comes from the anti-gravitating action of the dark side's cold matter once a discontinuous scale-factor permutation has made its source term dominant, not from gravitational collapse of the conjugate universe and not from dual kinetic energy carried across as Λ by w_eff = −w̃; the dark side contracts throughout, including our decelerating era. The result is power-law acceleration a ~ t′², not a cosmological constant.

findings.summary: Earliest Dark Gravity cosmology found. Two time-reversal-conjugate metrics, with g̃_μν identified with g^μν in a privileged frame, give a pair of conjugate universes whose scale factors map as a → 1/a under t → −t. The coupled equation gives a ~ t² for our side, so 'our universe is accelerated without any need for a cosmological constant or dark energy component'; the model is fitted to the supernova data of the time.
findings.difference: Here the acceleration is pure geometry of the coupled conjugate metrics and, in the paper's words, independent of the matter in either universe, so the conjugate side's contents, and any collapse of them, play no role. The conjugate universe is a time-reversed partner, not the momentum-space description of ours; power law a ~ t², not Λ.

findings.citation: H. Wu, H. Yang, "Double Field Theory Inspired Cosmology", JCAP 07 (2014) 024, arXiv:1307.0159
findings.summary: Cosmological solutions of double field theory, which doubles space into ordinary coordinates x and dual (T-dual) coordinates x̃. In the solution with an O(D,D)-invariant dilaton potential the dual scale factor is the inverse of the ordinary one, a₂ = a⁻¹, so the dual space contracts while ordinary space expands. The authors state that the contraction of the dual space causes the ordinary space first to inflate (accelerate) and later to expand at a decelerating rate. A later DFT paper (Y. Liu, Gen. Rel. Grav. 54 (2022) 18, arXiv:2112.15082) summarizes the result as 'the contraction of the conjugated space leads to both an inflation phase and a decelerated expansion of the ordinary space'.
findings.difference: Same causal wording as C5 (contraction of the dual space, with the inverse scale factor, accelerates our space), but for primordial inflation, not the present acceleration. The dual space is the winding (T-dual) coordinate space of double field theory, not the momentum-space polarization of a Born-reciprocal theory. The driver is dilaton dynamics with an exponential potential; no matter content, no collapse of a conjugate sector, no dictionary entry such as dual stiff → Λ. The same contraction also produces the later decelerated expansion, so in this paper contraction alone does not fix the sign of the acceleration; with a₂ = a⁻¹ the 'causes' is a kinematic identity of one solution.

findings.citation: M. Gasperini, G. Veneziano, "The pre-big bang scenario in string cosmology", Phys. Rept. 373 (2003) 1, arXiv:hep-th/0207130
findings.summary: In pre-big-bang cosmology one evolution is described in two conformal frames. A superinflationary (accelerating) expansion in the string frame is an accelerated contraction in the Einstein frame, where the dilaton is a massless scalar minimally coupled to gravity (kinetic-dominated, a stiff fluid) that cannot inflate but 'can easily lead to gravitational collapse'; section 3.3 is titled 'Pre-big bang inflation as gravitational collapse'. Section 2.2 also gives the scale-factor duality with sources, attributed to Veneziano 1991: a_i → a_i⁻¹ with the shifted density ρ̄ = ρ √−g preserved and the shifted pressure reversed, which 'reflects' the barotropic equation of state γ → −γ. This is the same map as the program's corrected dictionary w_eff = −w̃ (#11 section 10), which carries the energy per comoving volume across unchanged; under it a stiff fluid (γ = 1) goes to γ = −1.
findings.difference: The two descriptions are the string and Einstein conformal frames, related by the dilaton, not position and momentum related by Born reciprocity; the collapse is of our own universe as seen in the other frame, not of a conjugate one; the acceleration is primordial superinflation (growing H), not the present epoch and not a cosmological constant. The duality with sources is an exact symmetry of string-frame dilaton gravity, whereas the program derives w_eff = −w̃ in Einstein gravity from a·ã = 1 with one shared lapse; the paper never applies γ → −γ to dark energy. Read with C5's route, it states the same structure: a contracting, kinetic-dominated universe in one description is an accelerating universe in the other.

findings.citation: A. Buonanno, T. Damour, G. Veneziano, "Pre-big bang bubbles from the gravitational instability of generic string vacua", Nucl. Phys. B 543 (1999) 275, arXiv:hep-th/9806230
findings.summary: States the pre-big-bang reading of inflation as gravitational collapse: a generic string vacuum of incoming gravitational and dilatonic waves collapses gravitationally (Einstein frame) into black holes, and each collapse hypersurface becomes, in the string-frame metric, a big bang preceded by dilaton-driven inflation; it gives a criterion for 'collapse/inflation' in terms of asymptotic data.

findings.citation: S. Bolognesi, "A cosmology of a trans-Planckian theory and dark energy", Int. J. Mod. Phys. D 23 (2014) 1450046, arXiv:1207.5514
findings.summary: A theory built on Born reciprocity: the action is S + S̃, the second term written on a separate energy-momentum manifold with its own FRW-type 'dual universe' (scale factor ã(e) in the energy e), linked to spacetime by a generalized Fourier transform; x↔p duality sets the fundamental cosmological constant to zero. Inflation suppresses the dual sector until late times. When it re-emerges for cold dark matter, the dual action's 0–0 kinetic term in momentum space, transformed back to spacetime, becomes a negative mass-squared term, and the corresponding g_μν term in the dark-matter stress tensor is an effective positive cosmological constant, of the observed size if inflation lasts the minimal number of e-folds.
findings.difference: No contraction or collapse: the dual universe is an FRW universe in energy whose scale factor grows with e as ours grows with t, and the normalizations are tied by M² a = ã (2015 paper), not a·ã = 1. The acceleration is an effect of the dual action on dark matter's equation of motion, not the gravitational dynamics of a contracting conjugate universe; no w_eff = −w̃ dictionary. Shared with C5: the present acceleration is sourced by the momentum-space side of an x↔p-symmetric world, and a momentum-space kinetic term appears in spacetime as a vacuum-energy-like term (compare the route 'dual stiff → Λ').

quotes.text: We propose a scenario in which an effective positive cosmological constant is caused by how the dual sector of the theory affects the equation of state for matter particles.
The x\leftrightarrow p duality is, for us, the principle that sets \Lambda_{\rm fund}=0 .

The main result of the paper is that an effective cosmological constant term, which is compatible with the observed value of the universe acceleration, can be explained by the intervention of the \widetilde{S} part of the action on the dark matter equation of state.

findings.citation: P. Berglund, T. Hübsch, D. Minić, "Dark Energy and String Theory", Phys. Lett. B 798 (2019) 134950, arXiv:1905.08269
findings.summary: In a doubled, non-commutative (metastring, Born-geometric) formulation of string theory with dual coordinates x̃, integrating the doubled action over x̃ makes the size of the dual space set Newton's constant and its curvature set our cosmological constant: the curvature of 'the canonically conjugate dual space' induces the observed dark energy. Follow-ups state the same (LHEP 2021 186, arXiv:2010.15610: 'dark energy is generated by the dynamical geometry of the dual spacetime').
findings.difference: A static attribution: our Λ is the curvature (Einstein-Hilbert term) of the dual space, not the contents of a contracting conjugate universe; no contraction, collapse, a·ã = 1 dynamics or w_eff = −w̃ dictionary. The program's dictionary maps dual spatial curvature to dark radiation and the dual Einstein term to an a⁻⁶ step in G_eff (#11 section 10), so the two assignments differ. The doubled action goes back to Tseytlin 1990-91.

quotes.text: the curvature of the canonically conjugate dual space provides for a positive cosmological constant to leading order, that satisfies a radiatively stable see-saw-like formula, which in turn induces the dark energy in the observed spacetime
It also follows that the weakness of gravity is determined by the size of the canonically conjugate dual space, while the smallness of the cosmological constant is given by its curvature.

findings.citation: S. Hur, V. Jejjala, M. J. Kavic, D. Minic, T. Takeuchi, "Dynamical dark energy, dual spacetime, and DESI", JCAP 11 (2025) 054, arXiv:2503.20854
findings.summary: Dark energy 'stems from the curvature of the dual spacetime' of the metastring, and Λ/G_N 'will evolve together with the evolution of the x̃-spacetime'. The vacuum energy is an integral over dual energies between UV and IR cutoffs that depend on our scale factor a, using δx δx̃ ~ λ² to convert our volume to a dual one (so the dual cutoffs run inversely to ours, e.g. Ẽ_UV proportional to a); with infinite statistics this gives w₀, wₐ compared with DESI. The record cites this paper in wiki/papers/phase-space-diameter.md for another purpose.
findings.difference: Dark energy from the curvature of the dual spacetime, its evolution set by UV/IR cutoff relations, not from the gravitational collapse or contents of a contracting conjugate universe; no statement that the dual spacetime contracts and no dictionary w_eff = −w̃ (searched the full text for contract/shrink/collaps: none apply to the dual spacetime).

quotes.text: In our model, dark energy stems from the curvature of the dual spacetime

Thus, the weakness of gravity is determined by the size of the canonically conjugate dual \mathord{\tilde{x}} -spacetime, while the smallness of the cosmological constant is given by its curvature \tilde{R} .
Note that this expression also implies that \Lambda/G_{N} will evolve together with the evolution of the \mathord{\tilde{x}} -spacetime.

findings.citation: S. Ran, "Restoring a missing duality in quantum mechanics", Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 042203, arXiv:2511.20907
findings.summary: Gives the momentum-energy representation its own autonomous unitary evolution (Hilbert space H_xt + H_kE) and argues that a stationary, random-phase background of modes on the momentum-energy manifold, seen through the Fourier map, is a homogeneous, isotropic, constant energy density in spacetime, which the author identifies with the cosmological constant (dark energy).
findings.difference: Shares only the attribution of dark energy to a state living on the momentum side; there is no cosmology (no scale factors, no Friedmann equation, no acceleration computed), no contraction or collapse, and the density is a Fourier-projection identity rather than a gravitational effect. Weakest of the partial matches.

quotes.text: a stationary background on \mathcal{M}_{kE} projects into \mathcal{M}_{xt} as a uniform and isotropic energy density—dark energy
These are precisely the defining physical properties of a cosmological constant, or dark energy.
quotes.where: full text, section II.1 'Dark Energy from Pure Fourier Projection'

findings.citation: G. Veneziano, "Scale factor duality for classical and quantum strings", Phys. Lett. B 265 (1991) 287
findings.summary: Origin of scale-factor duality: the string-modified Friedmann equations have duality-related solutions under inversion of the scale factor. Gasperini-Veneziano 2003 attribute to this paper the duality with sources (their eq. 2.32, ref. [600]) that preserves the energy per comoving volume and reflects the equation of state, the same map as the program's corrected dictionary w_eff = −w̃.
findings.difference: A symmetry between two solutions of string-frame dilaton gravity, not a relation between two descriptions of one state; no dark energy, no conjugate collapse. The equation-of-state reflection was checked only in the Gasperini-Veneziano review; this paper's full text was not retrieved.

quotes.text: The string-modified, Einstein-Friedman equations are then shown to possess physically-inequivalent, duality-related solutions

findings.citation: L. P. Chimento, R. Lazkoz, "On the link between phantom and standard cosmologies", Phys. Rev. Lett. 91 (2003) 211301, arXiv:gr-qc/0307111
findings.summary: The 'phantom symmetry' of flat FRW: ρ̄ = ρ, H̄ = −H (so ā ∝ 1/a) and γ̄ = −γ for p = (γ − 1)ρ, i.e. w → −2 − w. This is the program's heuristic dictionary w_eff = −2 − w̃, which identified densities across frames (#1 section 6), and under which dual dust gives w = −2, the first failed version of C5. The paper notes the duality is identical to the pre-big-bang one.
findings.difference: A form-invariance map between two cosmologies, used to build phantom models; no conjugate universe and no claim that a contracting dual drives our acceleration.

quotes.text: This follows directly from the relationship \bar{H}=-H , which gives in turn \bar{a}\propto a^{-1} .
is identical to the one appearing in the pre-big bang models

findings.citation: M. P. Dąbrowski, T. Stachowiak, M. Szydłowski, "Phantom cosmologies", Phys. Rev. D 68 (2003) 103519, arXiv:hep-th/0307128
findings.summary: Finds, independently of Chimento-Lazkoz, the duality a → 1/a with γ → −γ (w → −(w + 2)) between standard and phantom flat models, and lists the pairs: dust is dual to a phantom with p = −2ρ, stiff fluid to p = −3ρ. The dust entry is exactly the w = −2 that the program's heuristic dictionary produced for dual dust.
findings.difference: Mathematical duality of flat FRW solutions; no conjugate description, no collapse-driven acceleration.

quotes.text: From these we can conclude that standard fluids like: dust \gamma=1 , radiation \gamma=4/3 , stiff-fluid \gamma=2 are dual to phantoms with \gamma=-1 ( p=-2\varrho )
quotes.where: full text, section III 'Phantom models duality'

findings.citation: U. Camara da Silva, A. A. Lima, G. M. Sotkov, "Scale Factor Self-Dual Cosmological Models", JHEP 07 (2015) 017, arXiv:1502.06497
findings.summary: A conformal-time scale-factor duality in Einstein gravity, ã = c₀²/a with w + w̃ = −2/3, maps expanding solutions to contracting ones and every decelerating matter or radiation phase to an accelerating dark-energy phase of the dual model; de Sitter is dual to the radiation universe. Used as a UV/IR symmetry relating the late de Sitter stage to the radiation era.
findings.difference: A third dictionary (w + w̃ = −2/3 rather than w_eff = −w̃), relating two different solutions rather than two descriptions of one state; no claim that the dual's contraction drives our acceleration.

quotes.text: we realize that the entire radiation, matter or DM dominated phases of decelerated expansion are always mapped into the corresponding DE dominated accelerated expansion periods in the dual model
the de Sitter universe ( \omega=-1 ) is dual to the radiation filled universe ( \omega=1/3 )

findings.citation: J. J. Levin, "Inflation from extra dimensions", Phys. Lett. B 343 (1995) 69, arXiv:gr-qc/9411041
findings.summary: In vacuum higher-dimensional cosmology the shear of n > 1 contracting extra dimensions inflates the three visible ones: 'the expansion of the 3-volume is accelerated by the contraction of the n-volume', equivalent after reduction to inflation powered by dilaton kinetic energy ('kinetic inflation').
findings.difference: The contracting space is a set of extra spatial dimensions, not a conjugate (momentum-space) description; the epoch is inflation; the driver is kinetic energy of the internal geometry, which echoes the record's kinetic-dominated route but without a dual frame or Λ.

quotes.text: Said another way, the expansion of the 3-volume is accelerated by the contraction of the n-volume.
A connection can therefore be made to recent examples of inflation powered by a dilaton kinetic energy.

findings.citation: A. A. Tseytlin, C. Vafa, "Elements of string cosmology", Nucl. Phys. B 372 (1992) 443, arXiv:hep-th/9109048
findings.summary: Records the duality intuition of Brandenberger-Vafa string gas cosmology: what ordinary (momentum-mode) matter does for the size of the universe, dual (winding) matter does for the dual size, so winding modes accelerate contraction and oppose expansion.
findings.difference: T-duality between momentum and winding modes acting on one compact space; it does not claim that a contracting dual drives our acceleration.

quotes.text: the dual matter (the winding states) should do for the dual size of the universe (i.e., accelerate contraction)

findings.citation: F. Ferrer, T. Multamäki, S. Räsänen, "Fitting oscillating string gas cosmology to supernova data", JHEP 04 (2009) 006, arXiv:0812.4182
findings.summary: In string gas cosmology the extra dimensions, pushed by matter and pulled back by the string gas, can oscillate during the matter era, producing late-time acceleration of the visible dimensions; fitted to supernovae, it is acceptable but disfavoured against Λ.
findings.difference: Late-time acceleration from the dynamics of hidden extra dimensions, not from a conjugate description; oscillation rather than collapse; no Born reciprocity.

quotes.text: can lead to oscillations of the extra dimensions and acceleration in the visible dimensions

findings.citation: J. K. Erickson, D. H. Wesley, P. J. Steinhardt, N. Turok, "Kasner and mixmaster behavior in universes with equation of state w >= 1", Phys. Rev. D 69 (2004) 063514, arXiv:hep-th/0312009
findings.summary: Bears on the open question #11 section 10 names, whether the contracting conjugate universe is kinetic-dominated: in a contracting universe a w = 1 (stiff, kinetic) component and anisotropy scale with the same power of the scale factor, so their ratio stays fixed; the contraction becomes homogeneous and isotropic (Friedmann) only for w > 1.
findings.difference: Standard contracting-universe dynamics in one frame; says nothing about a conjugate description or our acceleration. Relevance: a stiff-dominated contracting conjugate universe would carry anisotropy at a fixed ratio, while the record's dictionary is derived for homogeneous isotropic fluids only.

quotes.text: We show that chaotic mixmaster oscillations due to anisotropy and curvature are suppressed, and the contraction is described by a homogeneous and isotropic Friedmann equation if $w>1$.

Inspection of (8) reveals that, when w=1 , the matter density and the anisotropy terms in the Friedmann equation (12) scale with the same power of a , so \Omega_{\rho} and \Omega_{\sigma} remain fixed.

findings.citation: J.-P. Petit, G. d'Agostini, "Negative mass hypothesis in cosmology and the nature of dark energy", Astrophys. Space Sci. 354 (2014) (INSPIRE gives the page as 2106), doi:10.1007/s10509-014-2106-5, INSPIRE recid 1330154
findings.summary: Janus cosmological model: two coupled metrics for positive- and negative-mass species; in the non-steady solution the positive species accelerates while the negative one decelerates, so dark energy is replaced by the action of (dominant) negative matter. Petit, Margnat, Zejli, EPJC 84 (2024) 1226 restate it: our acceleration follows if the system's energy is predominantly negative.
findings.difference: Partner sector of negative mass drives our acceleration by repulsion; the partner decelerates (not stated to contract) and is a time-reversed twin, not a conjugate (momentum-space) description; no collapse, no Λ from kinetic energy. Full text not read (publisher login); the label rests on the abstract and the 2024 restatement.

quotes.text: We build a non-steady solution where the positive species accelerates while the negative one decelerates. So that dark energy is replaced by (dominant) negative matter action.

findings.citation: A. D. Linde, "The Universe Multiplication and the Cosmological Constant Problem", Phys. Lett. B 200 (1988) 272
findings.summary: Two globally interacting universes with positive- and negative-energy particles; the effective cosmological constant in each vanishes automatically.
findings.difference: Partner universe used to cancel Λ, not to produce acceleration; no collapse or conjugate description. Kaplan-Sundrum 2005 (hep-th/0505265, a ghost copy of the Standard Model under Energy → −Energy) is of the same kind.

quotes.text: whereas the effective cosmological constant in each of the universes vanishes automatically

findings.citation: H. Falomir, J. Gamboa, F. Méndez, P. Gondolo, "Inflation without Inflaton: A Model for Dark Energy", Phys. Rev. D 96 (2017) 083534, arXiv:1707.04670
findings.summary: Two causally disconnected FLRW regions with scale factors a and b are coupled by a deformed Poisson bracket between their canonical momenta; the modified Friedmann equations acquire a source whose equation of state shows dark energy, with accelerating and decelerating regimes that can alternate.
findings.difference: A second universe acts on ours through momentum-sector noncommutativity of the scale-factor dynamics, not as the conjugate description; no contraction-driven acceleration or a·ã = 1.

quotes.text: The analysis of the equation of state clearly shows the presence of dark energy.

findings.citation: N. Kumar, "On the Accelerated Expansion of the Universe", Grav. Cosmol. 30 (2024) 85, arXiv:2406.04392
findings.summary: Assuming the universe is created as an entangled universe-antiuniverse pair with opposite time flow, the quantum focusing conjecture is used to argue that both expand at an accelerating rate, without dark energy.
findings.difference: Partner universe with reversed time implies acceleration through entanglement and quantum focusing; no contraction or collapse of the partner, no momentum-space description.

quotes.text: Assuming the validity of this hypothesis, in this paper, we show that the universe expands in an accelerated manner.

findings.citation: A. A. Tseytlin, "Duality symmetric string theory and the cosmological constant problem", Phys. Rev. Lett. 66 (1991) 545
findings.summary: Proposes an effective action S/V, motivated by a duality-symmetric closed string theory with independent coordinates x and their duals x̃, whose gravitational equation does not depend on the cosmological constant in S. Precursor of the Berglund-Hübsch-Minić dual-spacetime dark energy.
findings.difference: Concerns the value of the cosmological constant, not acceleration from a contracting dual.

quotes.text: The resulting gravitational equation is independent of the value of the cosmological constant that is present in S.

findings.citation: D. Farrah, K. S. Croker, G. Tarlé, V. Faraoni et al., "Observational Evidence for Cosmological Coupling of Black Holes and its Implications for an Astrophysical Source of Dark Energy", Astrophys. J. Lett. 944 (2023) L31, arXiv:2302.07878
findings.summary: Proposes that black holes formed by stellar collapse are the source of dark energy: if their gravitating mass grows with the scale factor (cosmological coupling), the black-hole population contributes a constant energy density, and the continuity equation then makes it vacuum energy. The scaling argument (energy per comoving volume growing so that density stays constant, hence w = −1) parallels the record's derivation of dual stiff → Λ.
findings.difference: The collapse is of stars into black holes inside our own universe, not of a conjugate universe; the coupling of black-hole mass to expansion is the disputed assumption (constraints against it: Rodriguez 2023, arXiv:2302.12386; Andrae and El-Badry 2023, arXiv:2305.01307).

quotes.text: The continuity equation then requires that black holes contribute cosmologically as vacuum energy.
We thus propose that stellar remnant black holes are the astrophysical origin of dark energy

findings.citation: E. Gaztañaga, "The Cosmological Constant as Event Horizon", Symmetry 14 (2022) 300, arXiv:2202.00641
findings.summary: Black Hole Universe: our universe expands inside its own Schwarzschild radius, possibly formed by the collapse of a free-falling cloud; the cosmological constant is read as the event horizon (a causal boundary term), so the observed acceleration needs no dark energy.
findings.difference: Collapse of a parent cloud in ordinary position space and a horizon read as Λ; no conjugate description or dual dictionary.

quotes.text: which could have originated from a uniform free falling cloud of mass $M$ that collapsed as a Black Hole (BH) 25 Gyrs ago

findings.citation: Planck Collaboration (N. Aghanim et al.), "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters", Astron. Astrophys. 641 (2020) A6, arXiv:1807.06209
findings.summary: With wₐ fixed to 0 (constant w), Planck combined with supernovae and BAO gives w₀ = −1.028 ± 0.031, consistent with a cosmological constant. This is a published measurement against the first, heuristic version of C5, which required dark energy with w = −2; the record states that 'the data exclude' w = −2 without citing a measurement (wiki page, #11 section 10).
findings.difference: Weighs only against the w = −2 version, which the record already treats as failed; it does not bear on the remaining route, which gives w = −1 if the conjugate contents are exactly stiff.

quotes.text: Also combining with Type Ia supernovae (SNe), the dark-energy equation of state parameter is measured to be w_{0}=-1.03\pm 0.03 , consistent with a cosmological constant.
Fixing the evolution parameter w_{a}=0 , we obtain the tight constraint
quotes.where: full text, dark-energy section, before eq. (48) (w0 = -1.028 +- 0.031, Planck TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+SNe+BAO)

findings.citation: A. S. Majumdar, D. Home, "Dark energy from quantum wave function collapse of dark matter", Phys. Lett. B 679 (2009) 167, arXiv:gr-qc/0506108
findings.summary: 'Collapse' here is dynamical wave-function collapse: energy liberated by collapse models acting on dark-matter wave functions accumulates into dark energy with w approaching −1.
findings.difference: Quantum-measurement collapse, not gravitational collapse; no conjugate universe.

quotes.text: Further, the equation of state for the liberated energy approaches w \to -1 asymptotically, providing a mechanism to generate the present acceleration of the universe.

findings.citation: T. Josset, A. Perez, D. Sudarsky, "Dark Energy from Violation of Energy Conservation", Phys. Rev. Lett. 118 (2017) 021102, arXiv:1604.04183
findings.summary: In unimodular gravity, energy non-conservation from non-unitary (collapse-type) modifications of quantum mechanics or Planck-scale discreteness accumulates into an effective cosmological constant.
findings.difference: Collapse in the sense of objective-collapse quantum mechanics; no gravitational collapse, no conjugate sector.

quotes.text: and it leads to the emergence of an effective cosmological constant in Einstein

findings.citation: G. Veneziano, J. Wosiek, "Exploring an S-matrix for gravitational collapse. II. A Momentum space analysis", JHEP 09 (2008) 024, arXiv:0805.2973
findings.summary: 'Gravitational collapse' and 'momentum space' together, but for transplanckian two-body scattering: a momentum-space formulation of an S-matrix approaching black-hole formation.
findings.difference: Black-hole formation in particle collisions analysed in momentum space; no cosmology, no conjugate universe.

quotes.text: the momentum-space formulation leads to an easier computation of the emitted-graviton spectra and to an attempt to study the system beyond its critical points into the presumed gravitational-collapse regime

findings.citation: J. Wang, Y. Xue, L. Chen, R. Zhang, "Dual Phonon Universe in a Spinor Bose Gas", arXiv:2503.20267 (2025); arXiv preprint only
findings.summary: Analogue gravity: two phonon modes of a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate see different effective metrics, and ramping the interspecies interaction makes 'one universe expand' while 'the other contracts'.
findings.difference: Laboratory analogue spacetimes for phonons; 'dual universe' and 'contracts while the other expands' in a different sense.

quotes.text: we observe that one universe expands, and in the mean time, the other contracts

closest.why: Overall closest: the only work found (Henry-Couannier's Dark Gravity, from gr-qc/0507065 in 2005 to PoS EDSU2018 047) that states, for the present epoch, a conjugate universe whose scale factor is the inverse of ours (ã = 1/a), contracting while ours expands, with the conjugate side driving our recent acceleration in place of a cosmological constant. It differs in what is conjugate (the inverse metric of a flat-background theory, a time-reversed twin with anti-gravitating matter, not the momentum-space description of our universe), in the driver (dominance of the dark side's cold matter after a postulated discontinuous permutation of the scale factors, not gravitational collapse and not dual kinetic energy acting as Λ through w_eff = −w̃), and in the result (power law a ~ t′², not Λ).

Closest on the causal wording: in double field theory, with the dual scale factor a₂ = 1/a, 'the contraction of the dual space automatically leads to' an inflation phase of ordinary space. It differs in epoch (primordial inflation, not today's acceleration), in the dual space (T-dual winding coordinates, not momentum space), in the driver (dilaton dynamics, no matter content or dictionary), and the same contraction later gives decelerated expansion.

Closest inside Born reciprocity: the momentum-space (dual) sector of an x↔p-symmetric theory produces the present acceleration, its momentum-space kinetic term appearing in spacetime as a vacuum-energy-like term. It has no contraction or collapse (the dual universe grows with energy as ours with time; no a·ã = 1) and acts through dark matter's equation of state.

Closest statement that collapse in one description is accelerated expansion in the other, with kinetic-dominated (stiff) contents on the collapsing side, and the source of the corrected dictionary's form (scale-factor duality with sources reflects γ → −γ with energy per comoving volume preserved). It differs in the pair of descriptions (string and Einstein conformal frames), the epoch (pre-big-bang superinflation) and the absence of Λ or a conjugate universe.

not_found.statement: C5 in its own terms: the momentum-space (Born-reciprocal, conjugate-polarization) description of our universe, whose scale factor is the inverse of ours (a·ã = 1), contracts as ours expands, and its gravitational collapse is what drives our present accelerated expansion. No paper found states this. The configuration (inverse scale factor, contracting partner, partner drives present acceleration) appears only in Dark Gravity, with a different partner and mechanism; the causal phrase 'contraction of the dual space ... inflation' appears only for primordial inflation (Wu-Yang 2014); dark energy sourced on the momentum or dual side appears without any contraction (Bolognesi 2012/2015; Berglund-Hübsch-Minić 2019; Hur et al. 2025; Ran 2026).

not_found.statement: The route the record keeps: a stiff (kinetic-dominated) fluid in a dual, conjugate or contracting sector acting on our expansion as a cosmological constant (dual stiff → Λ) as an explanation of present dark energy. The map itself exists in the literature as scale-factor duality with sources (γ → −γ, Veneziano 1991 via Gasperini-Veneziano 2003 eq. 2.32), and pre-big-bang cosmology identifies a collapsing stiff Einstein-frame universe with string-frame inflation, but no paper found applies the stiff → Λ entry to late-time dark energy.

search.notes: Group g4-collapse-acceleration, conjecture C5 only. Read first: wiki/cosmology/scale-factor-duality/collapse-powered-expansion.md, #11 section 10 and App. A items 6-9, notes/broken-born-theory.md sections 0 and 6. Result: no paper states C5 (the momentum-space description of our universe, with a·ã = 1, contracting and its collapse driving our present acceleration). Three partial strands exist and should be named when stating what is new: (1) Dark Gravity (Henry-Couannier 2005-2018) has the configuration - conjugate inverse-metric universe with ã = 1/a, contracting while ours expands, driving our recent acceleration without Λ - but the partner is a time-reversed twin with anti-gravitating matter, the driver is a postulated scale-factor permutation, and the outcome is a ~ t²; its venues are an arXiv preprint, a living review (Global J. Sci. Front. Res. A 2013) and PoS proceedings; the 2005 companion astro-ph/0509092 is withdrawn. (2) Contraction of another space accelerating ours, for inflation: Wu-Yang 2014 (DFT dual space, a₂ = 1/a), pre-big-bang inflation as Einstein-frame gravitational collapse of a stiff/kinetic universe (Buonanno-Damour-Veneziano 1999; Gasperini-Veneziano 2003), Levin 1995 (extra dimensions). (3) Dark energy sourced on the momentum or dual side without contraction: Bolognesi 2012/2015 (Born reciprocity; dual kinetic term → Λ-like term), Berglund-Hübsch-Minić 2019 and Hur et al. 2025 (dual-spacetime curvature), Ran 2026 (Fourier projection of a momentum-energy background). Dictionary finding, outside C5 proper but on its route: the corrected dictionary w_eff = −w̃ with the energy per comoving volume carried across is the scale-factor duality with sources of string cosmology (Veneziano 1991; Gasperini-Veneziano 2003 eq. 2.32, γ → −γ), and the superseded heuristic w_eff = −2 − w̃ is the phantom duality (Chimento-Lazkoz 2003; Dąbrowski-Stachowiak-Szydłowski 2003, where dust is dual to p = −2 ρ); #11 tags the dictionary [D - corrected en route] without these attributions. The program's derivation (Einstein gravity, a·ã = 1, one lapse) differs from the string-frame setting, where the map is an exact symmetry of dilaton gravity. Record already lists Bolognesi 2015 (review/closed-universe/analyses/observations.json) and cites Hur et al. 2025 and Berglund-Hübsch-Minić 2023 for other purposes; none was compared with C5 before. Hossenfelder 2008 (#11 ref. 25) was read: its FRW section makes no acceleration claim (exchange symmetry cancels vacuum energy), so it is not listed. Also checked and not listed: Mantz-Prokopec 2008, Chang-Minic-Takeuchi 2010, Freidel-Kowalski-Glikman-Leigh-Minić 2022/2023, Maldonado-Méndez 2021-23, Liu 2022 (DFT dark-energy candidates), Boyle-Finn-Turok 2018, Kaplan-Sundrum 2005 (folded into the Linde entry), Cai et al. 2007 and Chimento-Pavón 2006 (expanding/contracting dualities), Lidsey-Wands-Copeland 2000 (confirms the Einstein-frame dilaton vacuum is a stiff fluid). verdicts.reason: Confirmed partial. The proceedings state the configuration: the dark side, whose scale factor is the inverse of ours, contracts as ours expands, and after a postulated permutation its source term drives our recent acceleration without a cosmological constant (a(t') ~ t'^2). Not 'anticipates': (1) the conjugate is the inverse metric of a flat-background theory, a time-reversed twin with its own matter, not the momentum-space description; (2) the paper says the dark-side term dominates 'resulting from a(t) << ã(t)', i.e. because of the postulated permutation, and for cold matter the dark-side source ã^4 ρ̃ scales as ã, so it weakens as the dark side contracts (verifier's script dg_exponents.py, step 4): the contraction does not power the acceleration, and dark-side mass is felt on our side as negative mass; (3) the outcome is a power law, not Λ. The paper also mentions 'Another scenario leading to an exponential acceleration' (found in the verifier's extraction). Crossref metadata match (author given there as Frédéric Henry Couannier).

Downgraded to related. The paper's cosmological equation (its eq. 4) is source-free ('No source enters our cosmological equation except at the crossing time'), the scale factor is 'completely independent of the matter and radiation content in the two universes', and the claimed t^2 acceleration is the a >> 1 branch (eq. 7), where the term from our own metric (factor 3A, A = a^2) dominates the conjugate's (factor 3/A). The conjugate universe is neither said to contract nor shown to drive the acceleration, so no central part of C5 is stated; the paper shares the setting (a time-reversal-conjugate universe with inverse scale factor; acceleration without Λ). The 2006 review (gr-qc/0610079) moves the accelerated phase to the regime where the conjugate side dominates; that is the Dark Gravity statement that bears on C5.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed partial: the strongest Dark Gravity statement and the closest paper found for the founding image. In cold eras 'there is a dominant source term determined by the content of the side with greater scale factor'; for a << 1 the review's eq. (24) is (1/a)'' = const, so the conjugate scale factor ã = 1/a goes as t^2 with conformal time t -> 0-: in its own cosmic time ã ~ |T|^(2/3), a dust universe collapsing to a crunch, while ours accelerates as a ~ t'^2 (verifier's script, steps 1-3). Read kinematically this is 'their collapse is our acceleration' with dual dust, the version the program's corrected dictionary maps to dust. DG gets acceleration because its two sides share conformal time, which gives w + w̃ = -2/3 (w_eff = -2/3 for dual dust; step 8); the same inversion with a shared cosmic time gives the heuristic w = -2 (step 6). In the hot case a radiation-like contracting conjugate side gives our exponential (de Sitter) expansion ('The 1/t and t radiative eras solutions respectively translate into e^{t} and t^{1/2} evolutions', found; step 8), the route's structure with radiation in place of stiff matter; the review ties that phase to an inflation-like epoch. Not 'anticipates': the conjugate is the inverse metric, a time-reversed twin, not the momentum-space description; the review narrates the driver as the dominance of the conjugate side's matter, felt on our side as negative mass, not as collapse; making the accelerated phase late needs a postulated exchange of scale-factor regimes with reversal of the time arrow; the result is a power law. A reader could argue 'anticipates' for the founding image read as a kinematic identity, not for the record's route. new_findings.citation: D. Mukherjee, H. K. Jassal, K. Lochan, "Bouncing and collapsing universes dual to late-time cosmological models", Eur. Phys. J. C 84 (2024) 318, arXiv:2207.02835 (2022)
new_findings.summary: Uses the Jordan frame-Einstein frame correspondence to give the present, dark-energy-driven universe a dual description. An Einstein-frame ΛCDM universe always corresponds to a bouncing Brans-Dicke universe in the Jordan frame; quintessence plus matter always corresponds to a Jordan frame with a turnaround, a bounce or a collapse, decided by the evolution of the quintessence equation of state. The authors conclude that 'the effect of dark energy can equivalently be seen as collapse of space in a conformally connected universe' and speak of 'collapsing descriptions of the current accelerating universe'. It is the closest present-epoch statement found of #11's 'Their collapse is our acceleration' read as an identity between two descriptions of one universe (App. A item 8, 'synchronized, not causal'). It also bears on App. A item 7: thawing quintessence is dual to a Jordan-frame turnaround.
new_findings.difference: The dual description is a conformal (Jordan) frame of a scalar-tensor theory, related by a conformal factor set by the Brans-Dicke scalar, not the momentum-space description related by a·ã = 1. Dark energy (Λ or quintessence) is assumed in the Einstein frame and the Jordan-frame collapse re-describes it; the paper does not derive the acceleration from the collapse or from any conjugate contents, so C5's explanatory direction is absent. The turnaround 'can be tuned anywhere' with the Brans-Dicke parameter, so the collapse is not tied to the onset of acceleration, and for ΛCDM the dual is a bounce. No dictionary of the type w_eff = -w̃.

quotes.text: Therefore,the effect of dark energy can equivalently be seen as collapse of space in a conformally connected universe.

The effective bouncing and collapsing descriptions of the current accelerating universe may have interesting implications for the evolutions of perturbations and quantum fluctuations in the cosmological background.
quintessence models of dark energy with non-relativistic matter component are shown to be always dual to a Brans-Dicke Jordan frame with a turn-around, i.e., a bounce or a collapse.
The point of the Jordan frame turn-around for all the cases can be tuned anywhere by choosing an appropriate Brans-Dicke parameter.
These results indicate that the effect of dark energy can alternatively be realized as collapse of space in a conformally connected universe, at least classically.

new_findings.citation: D. Mukherjee, H. K. Jassal, K. Lochan, "f(R) dual theories of quintessence: expansion-collapse duality", JCAP 12 (2021) 016, arXiv:2105.10521
new_findings.summary: The first paper of the expansion-collapse duality line. It reconstructs f(R) Jordan-frame duals of quintessence-dominated Einstein-frame cosmologies and finds that, for a class of viable quintessence models, the Jordan-frame universe grows to a maximum size and then collapses while the physical (Einstein-frame) universe keeps expanding: a present-epoch expansion-collapse duality.
new_findings.difference: As for the 2024 paper: conformal frames of f(R) (scalar-tensor) gravity, not position and momentum; dark energy is assumed (quintessence) and the Jordan-frame collapse is a re-description, not a source; no inverse scale factor and no dictionary.

quotes.text: We show that for certain class of viable quintessence models, the Jordan frame universe grows to a maximum finite size, after which it begins to collapse back.
Thus, there is a possibility that in the late time limit where the Einstein frame universe continues to expand, the Jordan frame universe collapses.

new_findings.citation: M. Gasperini, G. Veneziano, "Inflation, deflation, and frame independence in string cosmology", Mod. Phys. Lett. A 8 (1993) 3701, arXiv:hep-th/9309023
new_findings.summary: The origin of the pre-big-bang identification that the searcher found in Gasperini-Veneziano 2003 and Buonanno-Damour-Veneziano 1999. String-frame inflationary solutions suggested by scale-factor duality are accelerated contraction ('deflation') in the Einstein frame, and the virtues of inflation have 'physically equivalent counterparts in the deflationary (Einstein-frame) picture'. One process, two descriptions: accelerated contraction in one is accelerated expansion in the other.
new_findings.difference: Conformal (Weyl) frames related by the dilaton, not position and momentum with a·ã = 1; primordial inflation, not the present acceleration; the contraction is our own universe's Einstein-frame metric, with no conjugate matter and no dictionary; superinflation, not Λ.

quotes.text: The inflationary scenarios suggested by the duality properties of string cosmology in the Brans-Dicke (or String) frame are shown to correspond to accelerated contraction (deflation) when Weyl-transformed to the Einstein frame.

We point out that the basic virtues of inflation (solving the flatness and horizon problems, amplifying vacuum fluctuations, etc.) have physically equivalent counterparts in the deflationary (Einstein-frame) picture.

new_findings.citation: C. Castro, "Born's reciprocal gravity in curved phase-spaces and the cosmological constant", Found. Phys. 42 (2012) 1031, doi:10.1007/s10701-012-9645-9 (not on arXiv)
new_findings.summary: Born-reciprocal gravity on the 8-dimensional cotangent bundle (curved phase space, Finsler nonlinear connection). A Kaluza-Klein-like construction yields the observed value of the cosmological constant, and the abstract links the geometry of momentum space to that value when momentum space is strongly curved and its size P is of order 1/R_Hubble.
new_findings.difference: Λ from the curvature and small size of momentum space: a static relation, with no contraction or collapse of a conjugate universe, no dynamics producing acceleration and no dictionary. Shares C5's theme (dark energy from the momentum side of a Born-reciprocal theory), like Berglund-Hübsch-Minić. The size P ~ 1/R_Hubble resembles the inverse scaling of a·ã = 1 but is not stated as a contraction. Full text not read (publisher); judged on the abstract.

new_findings.citation: C. Castro Perelman, "Born's Reciprocal Relativity theory, curved phase space, Finsler geometry and the cosmological constant", Ann. Phys. 416 (2020) 168143, doi:10.1016/j.aop.2020.168143 (not on arXiv)
new_findings.summary: Scalar-gravity solutions on the cotangent bundle in which the base spacetime and the internal momentum space are both (anti-)de Sitter; the solutions capture the early inflationary and very-late-time de Sitter phases, and regularizing the 8-dimensional phase-space action gives an extremely small effective cosmological constant.

new_findings.citation: A. Triantafyllopoulos, P. C. Stavrinos, "Weak field equations and generalized FRW cosmology on the tangent Lorentz bundle", Class. Quantum Grav. 35 (2018) 085011, arXiv:1903.12521
new_findings.summary: Generalized Friedmann equations on the tangent bundle, in which the curvature S of the velocity-space (vertical) part of the metric enters like a cosmological constant, so the accelerated expansion is attributed to the extra geometry.
