findings.citation: P. Sikivie, Q. Yang, "Bose-Einstein Condensation of Dark Matter Axions", Phys. Rev. Lett. 103, 111301 (2009), arXiv:0901.1106
findings.summary: Argues that cold dark-matter axions are driven by their own gravitational interaction to thermalize and Bose-condense: (almost) all axions go into one quantum state, with condensate patches about the size of the horizon, so the axions collect in one state while staying spread through space. In a homogeneous universe that state is the lowest momentum mode, which is condensation in momentum space in Einstein's sense. Continued rethermalization puts infalling axions into the lowest-energy state at fixed angular momentum (net rotation), which the authors use to explain caustic rings; the full treatment is Erken, Sikivie, Tam and Yang, Phys. Rev. D 85, 063520 (2012), arXiv:1111.1157. It is the closest published statement that dark matter collects collectively in momentum space through its own attraction.
findings.difference: Ordinary gravity plus Bose degeneracy drives the condensation; there is no attraction gated in relative velocity, no conjugate (p-polarized) sector and no Born reciprocity. The outcome is one condensate in the lowest-energy state, not a smooth Maxwellian fragmenting into a few discrete streams at different mean velocities. It holds only for highly degenerate bosons, the same requirement the record's classicality theorem reaches (#11 §9 (i)). The paper does not use the words 'momentum space'; equating Bose condensation with momentum-space clumping is the textbook reading and the notebook's own ('below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses — momentum-space clumping, realized', #1 §5.2). Its long-range coherence is disputed by Guth, Hertzberg and Prescod-Weinstein 2015 (evidence-against below). Citation graph: the 562 citing papers filtered for 'momentum space', 'velocity space', 'discrete flows' and 'condensation in momentum space' contain no statement of velocity-space fragmentation; the 35 references are the axion and BEC-halo lineage (Sin 1992/94, Böhmer–Harko 2007, Semikoz–Tkachev 1995).

quotes.text: We show that cold dark matter axions thermalize and form a Bose-Einstein condensate.
Axion BEC means that (almost) all axions go to one state.
Thus gravitational interactions cause the axions to thermalize and form a BEC
We expect overlapping condensate patches with typical size of order the horizon.

findings.citation: L. Berezhiani, J. Khoury, "Theory of dark matter superfluidity", Phys. Rev. D 92, 103510 (2015), arXiv:1507.01019
findings.summary: Dark matter made of eV-mass axion-like particles with strong self-interactions condenses into a superfluid core inside galaxies, where the velocity dispersion (and so the temperature) is low; in clusters, where the dispersion is higher, it is partly or wholly in the normal phase. In the condensed phase the dark matter behaves as collective excitations rather than individual collisionless particles. This is the notebook's form of C6, 'below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses', with 'superfluid-like cores in dwarfs' (#1 §5.2), and the same split between galaxies and clusters as the program's knee.
findings.difference: The condensate is a Bose–Einstein superfluid produced by strong contact self-interactions and Bose degeneracy, not by an attraction gated in relative velocity; there is one condensate, not several velocity streams; the aim is MOND phenomenology through phonons coupled to baryons; nothing is conjugate or momentum-polarized. Citation graph: forward citations filtered for 'momentum space' or 'velocity space' with 'condens' gave one unrelated thesis; the references are the BEC-halo lineage (Sin, Ji–Sin, Böhmer–Harko, Sikivie–Yang, Guth–Hertzberg–Prescod-Weinstein).

quotes.text: The condensate has a polytropic equation of state P~rho^3 giving rise to a superfluid core within galaxies.
due to the higher velocity dispersion in clusters, and correspondingly higher temperature, the DM in clusters is either in a mixture of superfluid and normal phase, or fully in the normal phase
Instead of behaving as individual collisionless particles, the DM superfluid is more aptly described as collective excitations.

findings.citation: A. H. Guth, M. P. Hertzberg, C. Prescod-Weinstein, "Do Dark Matter Axions Form a Condensate with Long-Range Correlation?", Phys. Rev. D 92, 103513 (2015), arXiv:1412.5930
findings.summary: Examines the Sikivie–Yang claim and argues that thermalization through attractive interactions (gravity, attractive self-coupling) produces localized Bose clumps (stars, solitons) with only short-range correlation; only repulsive interactions drive long-range order. A condensate forms, but it is not coherent over cosmological distances.
findings.difference: Weighs against the gravity-driven route to a condensate that is localized in momentum and spread through space, the published form closest to C6. It concerns attraction in position; it does not treat an attraction gated in velocity, whose Born-dual reading would localize in momentum rather than position, so it is not a test of the record's gated model.

quotes.text: there is an essential difference between the thermalization and formation of a condensate due to repulsive interactions, which can indeed drive long-range order, and that due to attractive interactions, which can lead to localized Bose clumps (stars or solitons) that only exhibit short range correlation
we conclude that while a Bose-Einstein condensate is formed, the claim of long-range correlation is unjustified

findings.citation: D. G. Levkov, A. G. Panin, I. I. Tkachev, "Gravitational Bose-Einstein condensation in the kinetic regime", Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 151301 (2018), arXiv:1804.05857
findings.summary: Shows with kinetic theory and simulations that light bosonic dark matter in virialized halos and miniclusters Bose-condenses through gravity alone, ending in Bose stars, and gives the condensation time. findings.difference: Collective condensation by an attractive self-interaction does happen for wave dark matter, but what forms is a lump localized in position (a Bose star), not streams spread through space and localized in velocity. No velocity gate, no conjugate sector.

findings.citation: R. Delbourgo, D. Lashmar, "Born reciprocity and the 1/r potential", Found. Phys. 38, 995 (2008), arXiv:0709.0776
findings.summary: Applies Born reciprocity to the 1/r potential: the Hamiltonian H = (p² + b²r²)/2m − α(1/r + b/p) gives the Coulomb or Newton attraction a reciprocal partner −αb/p, an attraction in momentum space. In a galaxy the pair interaction becomes GmM(1/r + Ω/|v − v′|), averaged over all other masses and their relative speeds; with Ω ≈ 1.5×10⁻¹⁵ Hz the extra term flattens rotation curves without dark matter. The momentum term changes how velocity follows from momentum (ṙ = p(1/m + bα/p³)), not the force.
findings.difference: This is the Born-reciprocal 'gravity in momentum space' that C6's mechanism needs (#1 §5.2's mean field with an attractive U(p − p′); App. A item 10), used as a mean field over co-moving neighbours in a galaxy. The authors draw no conclusion about matter clumping in momentum space; they use the term in place of dark matter, for ordinary matter. No collective instability, no conjugate polarization, no gate width.

findings.citation: J. G. Burgers, C. L. M. Mantz, T. Prokopec, "The Newtonian Limit of Hermitian Gravity", Gen. Rel. Grav. 45, 155 (2013), arXiv:0912.1517
findings.summary: In Hermitian gravity, a Born-reciprocal extension of general relativity to a complex manifold of space-time and momentum-energy (Mantz and Prokopec 2008), the field of a point mass integrated over positions obeys a momentum-space Laplace equation, ∇ₚ²φₚ ∝ M δ²(p) (eqs. 65–66), solved by a logarithmic potential in momentum: a Newtonian potential in momentum space, which the authors present as a realization of Born's reciprocity.
findings.difference: Gravity acting in momentum space in a Born-reciprocal theory, for a single point source only: no matter distribution, no clumping, no dark matter. The authors also report that this version of the theory misses light deflection by 25%.

findings.citation: C. B. Das, S. Das Gupta, C. Gale, B.-A. Li, "Momentum dependence of symmetry potential in asymmetric nuclear matter for transport model calculations", Phys. Rev. C 67, 034611 (2003), arXiv:nucl-th/0212090
findings.summary: Transport (BUU) models of heavy-ion collisions use a momentum-dependent mean field whose interaction term is ∫∫ f(r,p) f(r,p′)/(1 + (p − p′)²/Λ²) d³p d³p′ (eq. 10), with Λ a range in momentum; it is a simpler stand-in for the Gogny force, whose momentum dependence is two Gaussians in (k − k′). The single-particle potential (eq. 12) contains ∫ d³p′ f(r,p′)/(1 + (p − p′)²/Λ²), a potential set by the momentum distribution of neighbours at the same position. The form goes back to Gale, Bertsch and Das Gupta, Phys. Rev. C 35, 1666 (1987).
findings.difference: This is the mathematical structure of #1 §5.2's ε(p; f) = p²/2m + ∫U(p − p′) f̄(p′) d³p′ with U of momentum range μ, where ∇ₚU enters the particle velocity, and it has been standard in nuclear transport since 1987. The signs of the coefficients were not checked here. It is used for nucleons, with no dark matter and no claim of fragmentation into velocity streams. The notebook calls the structure 'Berry-curvature transport'; the nuclear momentum-dependent mean field is a closer established analogue.

findings.citation: S.-Y. Ha, E. Tadmor, "From particle to kinetic and hydrodynamic descriptions of flocking", Kinetic and Related Models 1, 415 (2008), doi:10.3934/krm.2008.1.415, arXiv:0806.2182
findings.summary: Kinetic (Vlasov-type) theory of the Cucker–Smale flocking model: each particle aligns its velocity with the others', weighted by a kernel in their spatial distance, and the velocity distribution concentrates onto one common bulk velocity ('flocking').
findings.difference: Velocity concentration produced by an interaction is the defining result of flocking theory, the source of the founding image's vocabulary ('flocking', 'murmurations'). The alignment is dissipative rather than a Hamiltonian attraction, is weighted by distance in position rather than gated in velocity, and drives the whole system to one velocity rather than several streams. Not gravity, not dark matter.

findings.citation: S. Alexander, S. Cormack, "Gravitationally bound BCS state as dark matter", JCAP 04 (2017) 005, arXiv:1607.08621
findings.summary: Fermionic dark matter with an attractive interaction (torsion-induced) undergoes a BCS transition; self-consistent superfluid halos are solved together with gravity, and dwarf-sized halos need a particle mass of about 200 eV.
findings.difference: A BCS-paired dark-matter halo exists as a model, matching the notebook's BCS analogy, but the pairing interaction is a contact attraction, not one gated in relative velocity, and the result is a superfluid halo, not velocity streams.

findings.citation: F. Xu, A. M. Wang, X. D. Yang, H. You, "Numerical Simulation Solution of the BCS Pairing Problem", Commun. Theor. Phys. 44, 171 (2005), doi:10.1088/6102/44/1/171, arXiv:quant-ph/0407100
findings.summary: Restates standard BCS theory: the reduced interaction pairs electrons of equal energy and opposite momenta and spins, (k↑, −k↓), and the attraction acts only within a shell of energies near the Fermi surface.
findings.difference: The notebook says 'a momentum-gated attraction is precisely the pairing interaction' (#1 §5.2). In BCS the attraction is restricted to an energy shell and pairs opposite momenta (relative momentum near 2k_F, zero total momentum), whereas an attraction gated to small relative velocity acts on the opposite set of pairs. This weighs against the BCS analogy as stated ('exact in structure'), not against momentum-space clumping. Any BCS textbook gives the same; this paper is the one whose text was checked.

findings.citation: P. Sikivie, I. I. Tkachev, Y. Wang, "The Velocity peaks in the cold dark matter spectrum on earth", Phys. Rev. Lett. 75, 2911 (1995), arXiv:astro-ph/9504052
findings.summary: Generalizes the secondary-infall model of halo formation and predicts that the cold dark matter velocity distribution at the Earth has discrete peaks: halo dark matter arrives in a set of discrete flows with distinct velocities. Natarajan and Sikivie, Phys. Rev. D 72, 083513 (2005), argue the discrete flows are robust; Erken et al. 2012 state that in the non-linear regime cold dark matter produces discrete flows.
findings.difference: The velocity structure is inherited from cold initial conditions (dark matter lies on a thin sheet in phase space that folds during infall), not produced by an instability of a smooth distribution under an attraction among co-moving particles. The flows are cold and narrow, not of width ~v*, and no new interaction is involved. It is a prior statement of the observable (dark matter in discrete velocity streams), not of the clumping mechanism.

quotes.text: The cold dark matter spectrum on earth is expected to have peaks in velocity space.

findings.citation: M. Zemp, J. Diemand, M. Kuhlen, P. Madau, B. Moore, D. Potter, J. Stadel, L. Widrow, "The Graininess of Dark Matter Haloes", Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 394, 641 (2009), arXiv:0812.2033
findings.summary: In the Via Lactea II ΛCDM simulation the local dark-matter velocity distribution grows clumpier with radius; at 400 kpc it consists of a little more than a dozen clumps in velocity space and no smooth component, which the authors attribute to large-scale streams from tidally disrupted subhaloes.
findings.difference: A structure like the founding image's 'O(10) macro-streams' (old row 3) appears in ordinary collisionless dark matter in outer halos, from accretion, with no new interaction. It bears on the test the momentum-gravity note proposes (§4: only about ten broad streams would test the image): such streams are expected in outer halos anyway, so a discriminating test would have to look at inner halos or at stream widths.

findings.citation: M. Vogelsberger, S. D. M. White, "Streams and caustics: the fine-grained structure of LCDM haloes", Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 413, 1419 (2011), arXiv:1002.3162
findings.summary: Follows fine-grained phase-space streams in the Aquarius haloes: about 10¹⁴ streams pass through a point 8 kpc from the centre, and the local velocity distribution should be very smooth, the most massive fine-grained stream contributing about 0.1% of the signal.
findings.difference: Ordinary cold dark matter, no new interaction; already cited by the record (momentum-gravity note §4). It is the baseline the founding image would have to differ from near the Sun: a smooth local velocity distribution rather than a few broad streams.

quotes.text: the velocity distribution of dark matter particles should be very smooth with the most massive fine-grained stream contributing about 0.1% of the total signal

findings.citation: P.-H. Chavanis, "Dynamical stability of infinite homogeneous self-gravitating systems: application of the Nyquist method", Eur. Phys. J. B 85, 229 (2012), arXiv:1002.0291
findings.summary: Nyquist analysis of the Vlasov–Poisson (Jeans) problem: for any symmetric single-humped velocity distribution the onset of instability is the same as for the corresponding barotropic gas; two-stream instabilities need double-humped distributions.
findings.difference: Under ordinary gravity a smooth single-humped distribution has no instability beyond Jeans that would create velocity streams. The record already cites it (momentum-gravity run 2) and computed the gated case itself; the paper does not treat an attraction gated in velocity.

quotes.text: We show that this result is true for any symmetric single-humped velocity distribution, not only for the Maxwellian.

findings.citation: C. Connaughton, C. Josserand, A. Picozzi, Y. Pomeau, S. Rica, "Condensation of classical nonlinear waves", Phys. Rev. Lett. 95, 263901 (2005), arXiv:cond-mat/0502499
findings.summary: Classical nonlinear waves (the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation) condense into a large-scale coherent structure below a critical energy density in three dimensions, a classical counterpart of Bose–Einstein condensation, described by wave-turbulence theory.
findings.difference: Condensation in wavenumber (momentum) space of classical waves, the regime that the record's classicality theorem allows for collective momentum-space behaviour (N_occ ≫ 1). Repulsive interaction, no gravity, no dark matter.

quotes.text: We study the formation of a large-scale coherent structure (a condensate) in classical wave equations
in analogy with standard Bose-Einstein condensation in quantum systems

findings.citation: L. Hui, J. P. Ostriker, S. Tremaine, E. Witten, "Ultralight scalars as cosmological dark matter", Phys. Rev. D 95, 043541 (2017), arXiv:1610.08297
findings.summary: Among the consequences of fuzzy (wave) dark matter: with cold dark matter most globular clusters in the Fornax dwarf should have spiralled to its centre, and fuzzy dark matter resolves this.
findings.difference: The consequence the notebook drew from velocity clumping ('the Fornax globular-cluster timing problem is a feature, not a bug', #1 §5.2; old row 4, under review) is published for wave dark matter, through cores and wave effects, without any clumping in velocity.

quotes.text: If the dark matter in the Fornax dwarf galaxy is composed of CDM, most of the globular clusters observed in that galaxy should have long ago spiraled to its center, and this problem is resolved if the dark matter is FDM.

findings.citation: L. Berezhiani, B. Elder, J. Khoury, "Dynamical Friction in Superfluids", JCAP 10 (2019) 074, arXiv:1905.09297
findings.summary: Computes dynamical friction on a perturber moving through a superfluid: a subsonic perturber ordinarily cannot lose energy, and the Jeans-like tachyonic mass of sound waves gives only a small nonzero friction.
findings.difference: Suppressed dynamical friction in condensed cores, a consequence the notebook drew from velocity clumping, is published for superfluid dark matter, from superfluidity rather than from velocity streams.

quotes.text: Ordinarily a subsonic perturber moving through a superfluid is kinematically prohibited from losing energy

findings.citation: M. Mehraeen, "Quantum Response Theory and Momentum-Space Gravity", Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 156302 (2025), arXiv:2503.06160
findings.summary: 'Momentum-space gravity' here names the quantum geometry (Berry curvature, quantum metric) of electron bands in multiband solids, written in gravitational language, including Einstein-like field equations in momentum space.
findings.difference: Same words, different thing: band geometry in crystals, not an attraction among particles in momentum space. A reader searching 'momentum-space gravity' meets this literature first.

quotes.text: We present a quantum response approach to momentum-space gravity in dissipative multiband systems

findings.citation: H. Yang, S. D. M. White, L. Gao, "The capture of halo material by orbiting subhaloes", arXiv:2602.23822 (2026), arXiv preprint only
findings.summary: 'Velocity space clumping' of halo stars is used for detecting subhaloes from stellar kinematics.
findings.difference: Same words, different thing: observational clustering of stellar velocities from accretion, not dark matter clumping in momentum space through an interaction.

quotes.text: Thus, initially starless subhaloes could not be detected through velocity space clumping of halo stars.

findings.citation: R. Delbourgo, D. Lashmar, "Born reciprocity and the 1/r potential", Found. Phys. 38, 995 (2008), arXiv:0709.0776
findings.summary: Writing Newtonian gravity in Born-reciprocal form, H = (p² + b²r²)/2m − α(1/r + b/p) with α = GMm, the interaction between two masses becomes GmM(1/r + Ω/|v − v′|): beside the 1/r term there is a reciprocal term that does not depend on separation and grows as the relative velocity falls, so bodies moving at similar velocities interact most strongly. Summed over a galaxy's masses and their relative speeds, the term flattens rotation curves without dark matter (Ω ≈ 1.5×10⁻¹⁵ Hz); the authors note that it weakens between galaxies receding in the Hubble flow. In the Hamiltonian the term changes how velocity follows from momentum (ṙ = p(1/m + bα/p³)), not the force.
findings.difference: A close variant in a different model: (i) it acts among all masses, as a replacement for dark matter, not among dark-matter particles only; (ii) it is an added term proportional to 1/|v − v′|, with no gate width v* and no dependence on distance, not a 1/r attraction multiplied by a gate W(|v − v′|/v*); (iii) it is non-relativistic and breaks Galilean invariance, which the authors list among their own criticisms; (iv) the authors make no claim about clumping. Its Hamiltonian behaviour is the record's 'Hamiltonian reading' (#1 §5.2; momentum-gravity note §2: 'A potential in momentum differences exerts no force'), and its Hubble remark parallels the note's Hubble-flow gating (§6). The record's null search (review/momentum-gravity/run2/analyses/clumping.json, C18) did not find it. Citation graph: 5 citing papers (Castro 2008, 2009, 2011; Pavsic 2009; Ghosh 2017), none develops the term; the 15 references (Born 1949, Jarvis–Morgan, Low, Govaerts et al., Milgrom) contain no earlier form of it.

might possibly offer an explanation for galactic rotation, without invoking dark matter

findings.citation: P. Schuster, N. Toro, K. Zhou, "Interactions of Particles with 'Continuous Spin' Fields", JHEP 04 (2023) 010, arXiv:2303.04816
findings.summary: For matter coupled to a scalar-like continuous-spin field, the leading velocity-dependent pair potential is L_int = (g²/4πr)[1 − (ρ²r²/32)(|vᵢ − vⱼ| − (vᵢ − vⱼ)·r̂)² + …] (eq. 129): a long-range interaction whose correction depends only on the relative velocity, vanishes for co-moving particles and for motion along the line joining them, and matters when ρvr ~ 1.
findings.difference: Already cited by the record (momentum-gravity note §9). The velocity dependence weakens the interaction for transverse relative motion at large ρvr, so the threshold velocity falls with distance rather than being a fixed v*; scalar current, not gravity; no dark-matter application.

quotes.text: Thus, at leading nontrivial order, the velocity-dependent potential for a pair of matter particles is
For particles moving along a line, the new term has no effect, while for transverse motion it becomes important at long distances

findings.citation: S. Kundu, P. Schuster, N. Toro, "First look at continuous spin gravity: Time delay signatures", Phys. Rev. D 113, 076017 (2026), arXiv:2503.03817
findings.summary: First linearized formalism coupling spinless matter to gravity mediated by continuous-spin gravitons (spin scale ρ_g); it computes only the time-delay signatures of gravitational waves in an interferometer, at leading order in Newton's constant.
findings.difference: No static or velocity-dependent two-body potential is computed, so there is not yet a gravitational counterpart of the scalar result above. It updates the momentum-gravity note's statement (§9) 'No gravitational (tensor) version exists': a linearized tensor version now exists, without the two-body force.

quotes.text: We develop a formalism for coupling spinless matter to continuous spin gravity at linearized level.
and is limited to leading order in Newton’s gravitational constant

findings.citation: J. Skolimowski, "Real-space analysis of Hatsugai-Kohmoto interaction", Phys. Rev. B 109, 165129 (2024), arXiv:2402.08557
findings.summary: The Hatsugai–Kohmoto interaction is diagonal in momentum space, which makes it exactly solvable there; in real space it has infinite range, its strength not depending on the distance between the interacting particles.
findings.difference: An interaction of unlimited range in position that is local in momentum (in the standard form of Hatsugai and Kohmoto, which was not read, it couples the two spin states of the same momentum): the structure of a momentum gate on a long-range interaction, in a solvable lattice-electron model. It is repulsive in the standard form, acts on electrons on a lattice, and is not a force law for dark matter.

quotes.text: it is exactly solvable in momentum space in any dimension
The attractiveness of this model comes also from the fact that it becomes diagonal in momentum space
The strength of the interaction is controlled by U and does not depend on the distance between the interacting particles.

findings.citation: A. Loeb, N. Weiner, "Cores in Dwarf Galaxies from Dark Matter with a Yukawa Potential", Phys. Rev. Lett. 106, 171302 (2011), arXiv:1011.6374
findings.summary: Dark matter interacting through a Yukawa potential has a velocity-dependent cross-section that makes cores in dwarf galaxies while leaving systems with much larger velocity dispersion, such as clusters, unaffected.
findings.difference: A dark-matter self-interaction that is effective only at low relative velocity, but collisional (scattering), not a long-range mean-field attraction; the record's own contact gate (#11 §8) belongs to this family (velocity-dependent SIDM; see also Feng, Kaplinghat and Yu 2010, Tulin, Yu and Zurek 2013, Kaplinghat, Tulin and Yu 2016).

quotes.text: could naturally explain the recently observed cores in dwarf galaxies without affecting the dynamics of objects with a much larger velocity dispersion, such as clusters of galaxies

findings.citation: R. Lasenby, "Long range dark matter self-interactions and plasma instabilities", JCAP 11 (2020) 034, arXiv:2007.00667
findings.summary: Dark matter interacting through a light vector mediator has a long-range self-interaction; coherent effects make small perturbations grow exponentially, as plasma instabilities do, at couplings far below the particle-by-particle limits. For velocity distributions with a single peak (such as an anisotropic Maxwellian) only magnetic instabilities exist.
findings.difference: Long-range forces among dark matter with collective velocity-space instabilities, but the force is a vector force (with its usual velocity dependence through magnetism), not gated by relative velocity. The single-peak statement agrees with the record's finding that a smooth distribution does not break into streams electrostatically (also Chavanis 2012). Already in the record's run-2 search (C18).

quotes.text: Coherent scattering effects through this force can lead to the exponential growth of small perturbations, in analogy to electromagnetic plasma instabilities.
For velocity distributions without multiple peaks (such as an anisotropic Maxwellian distribution), only magnetic instabilities exist

findings.citation: M. Costa, C. Creque-Sarbinowski, O. Simon, Z. J. Weiner, "Dark forces suppress structure growth", JCAP 06 (2026) 055, arXiv:2510.00098
findings.summary: Minimal models of scalar-mediated attractive forces between dark-matter particles do not enhance the growth of unbiased tracers: the faster growth of the density contrast is cancelled by faster dilution of the background dark-matter density, and CMB-compatible versions suppress structure growth.
findings.difference: A long-range attraction among dark matter only, but not velocity-gated; its main cosmological effects come through the background (faster dilution of the background dark-matter density), which the gated model lacks. This supports the momentum-gravity note's statement (§6) that the BOSS full-shape bound on scalar forces is set by the background modification and does not transfer to the gated model.

quotes.text: We show that minimal models of scalar-mediated forces between dark matter particles do not enhance the growth of unbiased tracers of structure

findings.citation: M. Kesden, M. Kamionkowski, "Galilean Equivalence for Galactic Dark Matter", Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 131303 (2006), arXiv:astro-ph/0606566
findings.summary: If dark matter feels a stronger self-attraction than baryons, stars gain energy preferentially during tidal disruption and the trailing tidal stream is enhanced; the roughly equal streams of the Sagittarius dwarf challenge differences in acceleration above about 10%.
findings.difference: A bound on an extra long-range attraction among dark matter only, not gated in velocity. For a gated force it applies at the satellite's relative speed; the momentum-gravity note (§6) maps it to ε ≲ O(1) (0.2–2.5) at v* = 120 km/s and finds it weaker than the Lyman-α forest. The record already uses it; listed here because its result weighs against the conjecture's required strength (ε > 1).

quotes.text: The Sgr dwarf galaxy is seen to have roughly equal streams, challenging models in which DM and baryons accelerate differently by more than 10%.

findings.citation: T.-T. Wang, Y.-G. Ma, Z.-Q. Zhang, "Effects of Ptot gates and velocity gates on light-particle momentum correlation in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions", Phys. Rev. C 99, 054626 (2019), arXiv:1909.06986
findings.summary: 'Velocity gates' and momentum gates are cuts on pair velocity or total pair momentum used to select particle pairs in femtoscopic correlation functions of heavy-ion collisions.
findings.difference: Same words, different thing: an experimental selection cut, not a force switched on by relative velocity. Most INSPIRE hits for 'velocity-gated' are of this kind.

quotes.text: The results indicate that momentum correlation functions gating with total pair momentum is stronger

closest.why: Sikivie and Yang 2009 is the closest published statement that dark matter, through its own attraction, collects collectively in momentum space while staying spread through space (axions Bose-condense by gravity into one state, with horizon-size condensate patches). It differs in mechanism (ordinary gravity plus Bose degeneracy, no velocity gate, no conjugate sector, no Born reciprocity), in outcome (one condensate in the lowest-energy state, not a smooth Maxwellian fragmenting into a few discrete streams of width ~v*), in scope (degenerate bosons only, which the record's classicality theorem also requires), and it never says 'momentum space'. Its long-range coherence is disputed (Guth, Hertzberg and Prescod-Weinstein 2015). For the condensed-core form specifically, Berezhiani and Khoury 2015 (1507.01019) is as close.

For the founding image's mechanism, a Born-reciprocal attraction in momentum space acting as a mean field among co-moving masses (#1 §5.2), the closest paper is Delbourgo and Lashmar 2007: Born reciprocity gives Newtonian gravity a partner term GmMΩ/|v − v′|, averaged over a galaxy's relative speeds. It differs in that it acts among ordinary masses as a replacement for dark matter and draws no conclusion about clumping in momentum space.

Delbourgo and Lashmar 2007 write the pair interaction of two masses as GmM(1/r + Ω/|v − v′|): a Born-reciprocal term, independent of distance, strongest for bodies with similar velocities, applied to galaxy rotation, with a remark that it fades for galaxies receding in the Hubble flow. It differs from C7 in acting among all masses (as an alternative to dark matter) rather than among dark matter only; in being an added 1/|Δv| term with no gate width and no 1/r factor, rather than a 1/r attraction multiplied by a gate W(|v − v′|/v*); in being non-relativistic and not Galilean invariant; and in making no clumping claim. Its Hamiltonian form changes the velocity–momentum relation, as the record's Hamiltonian reading does.

not_found.statement: No paper found that states that dark matter (or any matter) clumps collectively in momentum space by the Jeans mechanism with position and velocity exchanged: that an attraction acting between particles of similar velocity makes a smooth Maxwellian fragment into a few discrete velocity streams spread through space; nor any paper proposing that dark matter is matter of the conjugate (momentum) polarization that clumps in momentum space as ordinary matter clumps in position space. Momentum-space condensation of dark matter appears in print only as Bose–Einstein condensation or superfluidity (one state, degenerate bosons: Sikivie–Yang, Berezhiani–Khoury, Levkov et al.); discrete velocity flows only from cold infall or accretion (Sikivie et al., Zemp et al.); velocity concentration by an interaction only in flocking models (Ha–Tadmor); and a Born-reciprocal momentum-space attraction only without a clumping claim (Delbourgo–Lashmar, Burgers–Mantz–Prokopec).

not_found.statement: No paper found that proposes a long-range (1/r, gravity-like) attraction among dark-matter particles that acts only between particles moving at similar velocities, i.e. a relative-velocity gate W(|v − v′|/v*) on a gravity-like force, whether as dark-matter physics or as a modification of gravity. search.notes: Group g5 (C6, C7). No paper anticipates either conjecture. C6: two partials. Sikivie–Yang 2009: dark matter Bose-condenses by its own gravity into one state, coherent over horizon-size patches. Berezhiani–Khoury 2015: halo cores condense into a superfluid below a critical velocity dispersion, clusters stay normal. Both are Bose condensation of degenerate bosons, which the record's classicality theorem also says collective momentum-space behaviour requires; neither has a velocity-gated attraction, velocity streams or a conjugate sector. Guth–Hertzberg–Prescod-Weinstein 2015 weighs against the gravity-driven form (attraction gives position-space clumps, not long-range order). Mechanism relatives worth knowing for how C6 is described: the notebook's mean field ε(p; f) with an attractive U(p − p′) of momentum range μ is the standard nuclear momentum-dependent mean field (Gale–Bertsch–Das Gupta 1987; Das et al. 2003), closer than the Berry-curvature analogy the notebook gives; Born-reciprocal gravity in momentum space exists (Delbourgo–Lashmar 2007; Burgers–Mantz–Prokopec 2012), without clumping; flocking theory (Ha–Tadmor 2008) is interaction-driven velocity concentration. The BCS analogy as stated ('a momentum-gated attraction is precisely the pairing interaction') conflicts with standard BCS, which pairs opposite momenta within an energy shell (evidence-against, scoped to the analogy). Observables: discrete velocity flows are published for CDM from cold infall (Sikivie et al. 1995). Zemp et al. 2009 find about a dozen velocity-space clumps at 400 kpc in ΛCDM, so a test by 'about ten broad streams' (momentum-gravity note §4) would need inner halos or stream widths. The consequences the notebook drew (Fornax GC timing, suppressed friction in condensed cores) are published for fuzzy and superfluid dark matter (Hui et al. 2017; Berezhiani–Elder–Khoury 2019). C7: one partial, Delbourgo–Lashmar 2007 (Found. Phys. 38, 995 (2008)): Born reciprocity adds GmMΩ/|v − v′| to Newtonian gravity among all masses, distance-independent, strongest at small relative velocity, used for rotation curves without dark matter, with a Hubble-flow remark. Its Hamiltonian form is the record's Hamiltonian reading. The record's null search (clumping.json C18) missed it. Record updates for C7: Kundu–Schuster–Toro 2025/26 is a linearized continuous-spin gravity, so the momentum-gravity note §9's 'No gravitational (tensor) version exists' is out of date, though no two-body velocity-dependent gravitational force has been computed. Costa et al. 2026 supports the note's statement that the BOSS bound on scalar dark forces comes from background effects the gated model lacks. Leads for other groups, not labelled here: Hübsch and Minic 2026 (arXiv:2604.19418) argue that dual particles of modular spacetime model fuzzy dark matter and that every Standard Model particle has a dual fuzzy counterpart (C1, C4); Minic 2020 (2003.00318) and Freidel–Kowalski-Glikman–Leigh–Minic 2021 (2104.00802) identify the dual sector with dark matter (C1); Castro Perelman, Can. J. Phys. 97, 198 (2019), reads dark matter as an effect of Born's reciprocal relativity (C1); Bolognesi 2012/2015 (1207.5514, 1506.02187) gets an effective cosmological constant from the dual sector of a Born-reciprocal cosmology (C5). Process: STATE.md and the other groups' folders were not read. The arXiv API returned 429 once (logged) and was retried later. Every reported quote was checked with lit.py quote (all FOUND); the verdicts are in work/literature-check/g5-momentum-clumping/quotes.tsv. Working notes are in notes.md; queries.tsv is the raw query log.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed, for one form of C6 only. In a homogeneous universe the state is (a0†)^N|0>, every axion in the k = 0 mode, so 'dark matter condenses into one momentum state through its own gravitational interaction' is a fair reading, and the notebook itself calls halo condensation 'momentum-space clumping, realized' (#1 §5.2). What is distinctive in the founding image is absent: no attraction gated in relative velocity, no instability of a classical Maxwellian, one condensate rather than a few streams of width ~v*. The condensation comes from Bose statistics with gravitational relaxation and needs N_occ >> 1, the regime of the record's classicality theorem. The full text never writes 'momentum space', 'momentum-space' or 'velocity space' (grep, 0 matches). Its long-range coherence is disputed (1412.5930). It is not the earliest statement of this form: Riotto and Tkachev 2000 (new finding) have a Bose condensate forming in dwarf-galaxy cores.

Confirmed, for the notebook's condensed-core sub-claim: superfluid (Bose-condensed) cores in galaxies, and a normal or mixed phase in clusters 'due to the higher velocity dispersion', which matches #1 §5.2's 'below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses' and 'superfluid-like cores'. The mechanism differs (strong self-interaction and Bose degeneracy, not a velocity-gated attraction), and it makes one condensate, not streams. The paper's other velocity criterion (Landau's: infall velocity against the phonon sound speed) concerns dissipation in mergers, not a gate on a force, so it adds nothing for C7. Riotto and Tkachev 2000 state the condensed-core form fifteen years earlier.

Confirmed, within its scope. It argues that condensation driven by attractive interactions gives localized clumps with short-range correlation, against the gravity-driven, spatially coherent condensate of Sikivie and Yang, the published form closest to C6. It does not treat a velocity gate. Its logic agrees with the record's own result for a long-range gated attraction, whose added modes are 'spatial lumps carried by a velocity-selected population' (velocity-gated-gravity note §5), so it bears on attraction-driven momentum clumping in general, not only on gravity.

Confirmed. Gravitational condensation in virialized halos ends in Bose stars, lumps localized in position. The record already cites it as the method of the wave-island rate (#11 §9 (ii), 'LPT-style').

Confirmed. Les Houches 1999 lecture notes, a Springer book chapter (Crossref: doi:10.1007/3-540-45338-5_2). A secondary source for the textbook reading of Bose-Einstein condensation as condensation in momentum space. It shows that the phrase is not distinctive; it is not prior art for the founding image.

Confirmed, and it is the closest paper for C6's mechanism. Its Hamiltonian H = (p^2 + b^2 r^2)/2m - alpha(1/r + b/p) is reciprocity-invariant: the 1/p term is the Born dual of Newton's 1/r, and the harmonic term the dual of the kinetic energy. Summed over a galaxy's masses with <Omega/|v - v'|>, it is #1 §5.2's mean field int U(p - p') f(p') d^3p' with an attractive U proportional to 1/|v - v'|, acting through r-dot as the anomalous velocity does. It makes no clumping claim. The searcher's summary says the term 'flattens rotation curves'; the authors write that the fit is 'far from convincing' and that 'Born's idea will probably be found wanting' (both FOUND).

Confirmed. Eqs. (65)-(66) give a momentum-space Laplace equation for one point source, solved by a logarithmic potential in momentum, which the authors call a realization of Born's idea. It treats no distribution of matter and makes no clumping or dark-matter claim.

Rejected as irrelevant to C6. The paper reads matter and vacuum energy as momentum-space curvature and links a horizon to a curvature singularity of momentum space. It has no distribution of matter in momentum space, no interaction between particles in momentum and no clumping. Its subject is App. A item 10's (momentum space has its own gravity), which is not one of the conjectures checked here; with C6 it shares words only. Metadata: INSPIRE gives 2017, Crossref 2018 (vol. 15); the citation's 2018 is right.

Confirmed, and the sign the searcher left unchecked is attractive. Table 1 lists C_l = -11.70 and C_u = -103.40 (MDI), negative in all five parametrizations, with Lambda = 1.0 p_f(0) for MDI. Eq. (10) is then an attraction between nucleons at the same position, gated in relative momentum by 1/(1 + (p - p')^2/Lambda^2): the mean-field form of the record's own contact-range gated interaction (#11 §8), standard in nuclear transport since Gale, Bertsch and Das Gupta, Phys. Rev. C 35, 1666 (1987), the paper's ref. [1] (checked). No fragmentation in momentum is claimed.

Confirmed. Venue checked on Crossref (Kinetic and Related Models 1, 415 (2008)). Interaction-driven velocity concentration: dissipative alignment, weighted by distance in position, toward one flock. A closer mechanism relative is Ben-Naim, Krapivsky and Redner 2003 (new finding): an interaction gated in the difference of the variable fragments a uniform distribution into several discrete clusters.

Confirmed. Venue checked on Crossref (Phys. Rev. B 97, 165101 (2018)). An interaction-driven instability of a momentum distribution, in the Landau functional that has the form of #1 §5.2's eps(p; f). It deforms a Fermi surface; nothing fragments.

Confirmed. A BCS dark-matter halo exists as a model, matching the notebook's analogy by name; the attraction is a torsion-induced contact interaction, and the outcome is a superfluid halo, not streams.

Downgraded to related. The cited passages state textbook BCS: pairs of opposite momenta, with the attraction restricted to a shell. If the gate is on relative momentum (#11 §8's k), that contradicts the notebook's sentence 'a momentum-gated attraction is precisely the pairing interaction'. But it weighs against an analogy offered for C6, not against the claim that matter clumps in momentum space, so it is not evidence against the conjecture. The paper is a numerical-method paper; BCS 1957 or a textbook would be the better source. Metadata: the citation matches the journal version (Crossref: 'Numerical Simulation Solution of the BCS Pairing Problem', four authors); the arXiv version is titled 'Exact Numerical Solution ...' and lists a fifth author.

Confirmed. Discrete velocity peaks come from cold infall: a prior statement of the observable, not of the mechanism. The summary's side claim about Erken et al. 2012 checks: 'In the non-linear regime CDM produces discrete flows' (1111.1157, FOUND).
Confirmed. A useful caveat: a test by 'about ten broad streams' (velocity-gated-gravity note §4) would also be met by ordinary outer halos.
Confirmed. Already in the record (velocity-gated-gravity note §4; run-2 claim C18).
Confirmed. Already in the record (run-2 clumping analysis).

Confirmed. Venue checked on Crossref (Phys. Rev. Lett. 95, 263901 (2005)). Classical waves condense in wavenumber space with a defocusing (repulsive) interaction: the regime the classicality theorem leaves open.
Confirmed, as a shared consequence (the Fornax globular-cluster timing problem), not a statement of clumping.

Confirmed, as a shared consequence (suppressed dynamical friction in condensed cores). The paper itself finds a small non-zero friction for subsonic perturbers, from the Jeans-like tachyonic mass of sound waves.
Confirmed. 'Momentum-space gravity' here names the quantum geometry of electron bands.
Confirmed. 'Velocity space clumping' of halo stars, used as a way to detect subhaloes; arXiv preprint only.

Downgraded to related; still the closest paper found for C7. The Omega/|v - v'| term does not depend on position, so it adds nothing to p-dot: eq. (4) puts it in r-dot = p(1/m + b alpha/p^3) only, while p-dot = -r(b^2/m + alpha/r^3). The record treats this structure separately and finds that 'A potential in momentum differences exerts no force' (velocity-gated-gravity note §2). C7 is a different physical claim: a 1/r force among dark-matter particles, multiplied by a gate W(|v - v'|/v*), which pulls co-moving particles together in space (note §5). The two share a theme: an interaction of unlimited range, strongest at small relative velocity, applied to galaxies, with a remark on the Hubble flow. They do not share the physics: Delbourgo and Lashmar have no attraction in position, no gate width (a power law singular at zero relative velocity), and a term acting among all masses as a replacement for dark matter. The authors call their fit 'far from convincing' (FOUND). The record's null search (run-2 claim C18) does not cite it (checked).
Confirmed. Already in the record (velocity-gated-gravity note §9).

Confirmed. The full text has no 'static', 'Newtonian' or 'two-body' (grep); it computes only gravitational-wave time delays. So the update stands: a linearized tensor (continuous-spin gravity) formalism now exists, but no two-body force has been computed in it, against note §9's 'No gravitational (tensor) version exists'.

Confirmed. Venue checked on Crossref (Phys. Rev. B 109, 165129 (2024)). An interaction of unlimited range in position and local in momentum, in a lattice-electron model. The only attractive Hatsugai-Kohmoto papers found concern superconductivity (arXiv: 2 hits), and none applies the structure to dark matter or gravity (INSPIRE full text: 2 unrelated hits).
Confirmed. Collisional, velocity-dependent self-interaction: the family of the record's contact gate.

Confirmed. Supports the note's §6 reading that the BOSS bound on scalar dark forces comes from background effects that the gated model lacks.

new_findings.citation: A. Riotto, I. Tkachev, "What if dark matter is bosonic and self-interacting?", Phys. Lett. B 484, 177 (2000), doi:10.1016/S0370-2693(00)00660-2, arXiv:astro-ph/0003388
new_findings.summary: Self-interacting bosonic dark matter is put forward as a cure for cuspy cores and too many dwarf galaxies. In a virialized clump the phase-space density exceeds unity, so scattering is Bose-enhanced and the clump Bose-condenses. For v_e = 100 km/s, which the authors say approximately corresponds to dwarf-galaxy cores, the relaxation time is shorter than the age of the Universe above a stated coupling, and 'the Bose condensate in the center of gravitational well should form'. The paper then derives the core density that the condensate's self-annihilation allows. This is the notebook's 'below a critical velocity dispersion the core of a halo condenses' (#1 §5.2), in 2000.
new_findings.difference: It states the same form of C6 as Sikivie and Yang 2009 and Berezhiani and Khoury 2015, and states it earlier. The condensation comes from contact self-interaction and Bose statistics, not from an attraction gated in relative velocity. The result is one condensate in the core, not several velocity streams, and it needs degenerate bosons (the record's classicality theorem). The paper speaks of a condensate in the centre of the well, never of momentum space: reading it as momentum-space clumping is the notebook's identification, the same reading that makes Sikivie-Yang and Berezhiani-Khoury partial. Its relaxation rate (Bose-enhanced scattering in a virialized clump, after Tkachev 1991 and Semikoz-Tkachev 1995) is the kind of rate the record's wave island uses (#11 §9 (ii), 'Bose-enhanced, LPT-style'), without the gate. Its ref. [14], Tkachev, Phys. Lett. B 261, 289 (1991), was not retrieved (†).

quotes.text: One scenario which may be free of these problems invokes a self-interacting Bose-field.
However, with time the Bose-condensation will occur

which approximately corresponds to the parameters of the cores of dwarf galaxies

new_findings.citation: E. Ben-Naim, P. L. Krapivsky, S. Redner, "Bifurcations and patterns in compromise processes", Physica D 183, 190 (2003), doi:10.1016/s0167-2789(03)00171-4, arXiv:cond-mat/0212313
new_findings.summary: Agents carry a continuous variable. A pair interacts only when its two values lie within a fixed range, and both then take the average. A uniform initial distribution is unstable, with an instability that propagates in from the boundary in the continuum version and a 'negative diffusion instability' in the discrete one. It ends as a finite set of isolated, non-interacting clusters, equally spaced, with the spacing set by the interaction range. The authors relate the averaging step to one-dimensional inelastic collisions. This is the structure #1 §5.2 claims for dark matter: an interaction that acts only between near-equal values of a variable fragments a smooth distribution of that variable into discrete clusters, with widths and spacings set by the gate.
new_findings.difference: This is not matter, gravity or dark matter: the variable is an opinion, and the dynamics is a dissipative averaging, not a Hamiltonian attraction. Read as velocities, the averaging step is a totally inelastic collision allowed only below a threshold relative velocity. The record's tests cover the Hamiltonian cases. Streams spread through space are 'exactly neutral in mean-field dynamics in a homogeneous medium' (velocity-gated-gravity note §5), and elastic gated collisions 'still maximize entropy' (calc note #2, quoted on the founding-image wiki page). The compromise mechanism escapes both by dissipating energy. It is closer to the founding image's fragmentation into a few discrete streams than flocking (Ha-Tadmor), which ends in a single flock. No anticipation of C6 as a physical claim.

quotes.text: When the opinions of two agents are sufficiently close, they both acquire the average of their initial opinions; otherwise, they do not interact.
the system condenses into a finite set of equally-spaced opinion clusters
This behavior results from an instability that propagates from the boundary toward the center
Therefore, minute details of the initial conditions are magnified, ultimately resulting in isolated clusters.
Closely related averaging processes naturally arise in diverse systems, including one-dimensional inelastic collisions

not_found_assessment.reason: Holds for the founding image itself, with two qualifications. (1) Its condensed-core form was published before the searcher's earliest partial: Riotto and Tkachev 2000 have Bose condensation in dwarf-galaxy cores. Bosonic dark-matter halos go back further: Sin, Phys. Rev. D 50, 3650 (1994), on the halo as a Bose liquid (abstract read), and Tkachev 1986 and 1991 (†, not read). Every published form is one Bose condensate, not a few velocity streams from a gated attraction. (2) The clause 'velocity concentration by an interaction only in flocking models' is incomplete. Fragmentation of a uniform distribution into several discrete, equally spaced clusters by an interaction gated in the difference of the variable is established in compromise (bounded-confidence) dynamics (Ben-Naim, Krapivsky and Redner 2003), a dissipative, non-Hamiltonian setting; for velocities it amounts to inelastic collisions below a threshold. My own searches (velocity- and momentum-space instability, instability in or unstable in momentum space, gravitational instability with momentum space and reciprocity, dual matter and dual sector with momentum or velocity space, Born reciprocity with clustering or instability, a web search for a velocity-space phase transition of halos, Crossref on velocity-space Jeans instability) found no statement of the Jeans problem with x and v exchanged, nor of conjugate or dual matter clumping in momentum space. The dual-sector dark-matter papers named by the searcher (Freidel-Kowalski-Glikman-Leigh-Minic 2021, Minic 2020, Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2022, Hübsch-Minic 2026) contain no clumping, clustering or localization in a dual or momentum space (grep of full texts).

Holds, but the closest paper should be labelled related, not partial. Delbourgo and Lashmar's Omega/|v - v'| term depends only on relative velocity and exerts no force in position (their eq. 4; velocity-gated-gravity note §2). C7's defining feature, a 1/r attraction among dark matter switched by relative velocity, appears nowhere. My own searches (velocity-dependent long-range force; fifth force depending on relative velocity with dark matter; attraction at the same velocity with streams and long range; velocity-dependent gravitational constant for galaxies; interactions local in momentum and of infinite range applied to dark matter or gravity; attractive Hatsugai-Kohmoto; a web search for gravity depending on relative velocity among co-moving bodies; the citation graph of Delbourgo-Lashmar both ways, including Jarvis-Morgan 2005, which has no 1/p term) found nothing closer. A velocity criterion in superfluid dark matter (Berezhiani-Khoury: infall velocity against sound speed) concerns dissipation relative to the medium, a preferred-frame effect the note's §9 already covers, not a gate on a force between two bodies.

verify.notes: Verification of g5 (C6, C7). Read first: the two wiki pages, #11 §8-§9 and App. A, #1 §5.1-§5.2, and notes/velocity-gated-gravity.md §1, §2, §4, §5, §9, §10; the record's run-2 claim C18 was checked by grep. Not read: STATE.md, other groups' folders, round2/. Metadata: all 30 identifiers resolve, and titles, authors, years and venues match (the non-INSPIRE ones checked on Crossref). Quotes: the searcher's 56 quotes all FOUND on rerun, none loose; 15 further quotes of mine all FOUND (71 checks, 0 NOT FOUND; verify-quotes.tsv). Changed labels: (a) Delbourgo-Lashmar for C7, partial -> related. The term exerts no force in position, and the record classes such momentum-difference potentials apart from C7's gated 1/r force; it remains the closest paper for C7, and the closest for C6's mechanism. Both summaries also overstate the paper: the authors call their rotation-curve fit 'far from convincing'. (b) Xu et al. (BCS), evidence-against -> related: textbook BCS contradicts the notebook's BCS analogy, not C6. (c) Castro 2018, related -> reject: momentum-space curvature, not matter clumping in momentum space. Resolved open points: Das et al.'s momentum-gated term is attractive (all C negative in Table 1); Kundu-Schuster-Toro compute no two-body potential; Sikivie-Yang never write 'momentum space'; Erken et al. do say CDM produces discrete flows; C18 cites Lasenby and not Delbourgo-Lashmar. New: Riotto-Tkachev 2000 (partial, C6), the earliest checked statement of the condensed-core form; Ben-Naim, Krapivsky and Redner 2003 (related, C6), the fragmentation mechanism in a dissipative setting. Closest, as verified. C6 founding image (streams from a velocity-gated attraction): nothing states it. Its condensed-core form is published since at least 2000 (Riotto-Tkachev; Sikivie-Yang 2009; Berezhiani-Khoury 2015), always as one Bose condensate. Mechanism: Delbourgo-Lashmar 2007 (related). Fragmentation into discrete clusters: Ben-Naim, Krapivsky and Redner 2003 (related, dissipative). C7: Delbourgo-Lashmar 2007 (related). Leads not pursued: Sin, PRD 50, 3650 (1994; abstract read, no full text, no condensation claim in the abstract); Tkachev, Phys. Lett. B 261, 289 (1991) and Semikoz-Tkachev, PRL 74, 3093 (1995) (†, not retrieved).
